Ability.name: Splashworth's Glimpse
Ability.description: Involuntary flashes of memory from Splashworth's transplanted left eye. Triggered unpredictably, such as by the smell of salt water, certain angles of light through a viewport, or the sound of orders given in a voice that sounds too much like his father's. For a fraction of a second, Fluffington sees what Splashworth saw. He has learned to blink through them. He has not learned to stop them. He tells no one.

Character.name: Admiral Fluffington
Character.description: Current Admiral of the Puddle Navy. Pink felt, immaculately maintained. Commands the USS Fuzzball. Son of Admiral Stuffington (the war criminal he doesn't know is alive). Has Splashworth's transplanted left eye and experiences his memories. Studied at Naval Academy with Captain Snoot - their friendship broke over The Incident. Catchphrase: We sail where the puddles flow. Either complicit in the cover-up or in denial about his father's crimes. Last of the Stuffington line - House Stuffington's only living heir, though he doesn't know his father is alive. The family crest (three water drops and a felt star) adorns the USS Fuzzball's bridge. The weight of dynasty sits on pink felt shoulders.
Character.physicality: Pink felt, immaculately maintained. One transplanted googly eye (Splashworth's left eye).
Character.mentality: Does his job exactly as the Puddle Navy trained him to. Wakes up some nights seeing things he didn't live through. Getting harder to tell where the duty ends and the denial starts.
Character.background: Son of Admiral Stuffington. Naval Academy graduate. Rose to Admiral. Carries Splashworth's eye and possibly his guilt.

Character.name: Admiral Splashworth
Character.description: Legendary war hero of The Great Puddle War. Won the Battle of Damp Ridge against impossible odds. His tactics are still taught at the Naval Academy. Tried to stop the Moistened Valley Massacre and was killed by his own side on Admiral Stuffington’s orders. Officially remembered as dying heroically in battle . The truth is suppressed. His left googly eye was preserved and later transplanted into Admiral Fluffington, carrying fragments of his consciousness..
Character.mentality: Saw the battlefield clearer than anyone above him. When it mattered most, he chose right over orders. That's why they killed him.
Character.background: Won the Battle of Damp Ridge. Murdered at Moistened Valley while trying to prevent a massacre of surrendering Dry Ones. Death covered up by Treaty of Soft Landings.

Character.name: Admiral Stuffington
Character.description: Admiral Fluffington's father. Ordered the Moistened Valley Massacre - attacking surrendering Dry Ones forces despite Treaty terms being agreed. When Admiral Splashworth tried to stop the slaughter, Stuffington had him killed. Status: alive in The Locked Room on Feltropolis Level 7, imprisoned by the Treaty Council for 200 years. Fluffington doesn't know his father is alive..
Character.background: High-ranking Puddle Navy Admiral during The Great Puddle War. Wanted the Dry Ones destroyed, not integrated. Committed war crime that the Treaty of Soft Landings was built to cover up.
Character.motivations: Sought complete destruction of the Dry Ones rather than peaceful integration.
Character.reputation: Officially: deceased war hero. Unofficially: war criminal whose actions are suppressed.

Character.name: Captain Snoot
Character.description: Rogue explorer, smuggler, truth-knower. Faded blue felt. Missing one googly eye (lost in Snack Nebula crash - replacement may be the Googly Eye of Truth). Left the Puddle Navy after The Incident (~Year 120) when he discovered evidence of the Moistened Valley Massacre cover-up. Carries proof hidden somewhere. Drinks at The Soggy Sock. Trades with Cookie Pirates. The rivalry with Fluffington isn't petty - it's about institutional truth vs loyalty. In Year 203 YSL, Snoot discovered The Rolling Pin past the Crumblefields - a humming Bakerfolk ruin three kilometers long. He brought back a fragment that resonates with the Eternal Drip's pump cycle. Uses Madame Threadbare at The Thread Market as an information source, playing both sides of the intelligence game.
Character.physicality: Faded blue felt. One missing googly eye with eyepatch (may contain Googly Eye of Truth).
Character.mentality: Drinks too much, trusts too little, and is right about almost everything. Left the Navy with the truth and never figured out what to do with it. Still hasn't.
Character.background: Naval Academy graduate. Discovered massacre evidence. Left navy under mysterious circumstances (The Incident). Now a rogue explorer and smuggler.
Character.reputation: Disgraced ex-officer to the establishment. Folk hero to those who suspect the truth.

Character.name: Chief Engineer Wrinkless
Character.description: Chief Engineer on the USS Fuzzball. Very old with faded brown felt. Served under Admiral Splashworth himself. Knows things about the old days. During the Crumblefield Standoff (Year 197 YSL), Wrinkles was the one who stopped Admiral Fluffington from firing on the Stale Vengeance by pointing out the compressed sugar particulates would chain-detonate and destroy both ships. Possibly saved everyone aboard both vessels.
Character.background: Served under Admiral Splashworth during The Great Puddle War.

Character.name: Commander Vera
Character.description: Possible Claw agent on the USS Fuzzball. Cold and efficient. Rumored to have Claw connections. Either reports on Fluffington's loyalty to the intelligence organization, or is actually loyal to Fluffington and lying to the Claw.
Character.mentality: Doesn't waste words or loyalty. Maybe reports on Fluffington to The Claw, maybe doesn't. Either way, she's the most dangerous person on the Fuzzball.

Character.name: Commander Vex
Character.description: Mentioned in Puddle Navy records but personality undeveloped.

Character.name: Doc Stitch
Character.description: Medical Officer on the USS Fuzzball. White felt. Specializes in felt repair and googly eye maintenance.

Character.name: Drizzle
Character.description: Bartender at The Soggy Sock tavern on Feltropolis Level 3. War veteran who lost her color from trauma - was purple, now gray. One of the oldest living moppets at around 260 years old (born 60 BT). Witnessed the Moistened Valley Massacre - saw Splashworth killed by his own side. Won't speak about it. Waters Snoot's drinks because she actually likes him. Arranged Snoot's eye replacement at Feltropolis. Sends Admiral Fluffington a drink every Year Zero anniversary - he never touches it. Filed the Soggy Sock Incident Report, Year 203 YSL, when Snoot arrived with a Bakerfolk fragment and a feral moppet on a leash. Noticed that Madame Threadbare's faded violet felt might be partial decoloration - takes one to know one.
Character.physicality: Gray felt, formerly purple before traumatic decoloration
Character.mentality: She was at Moistened Valley. She doesn't talk about it. She waters Snoot's drinks because she needs him alive more than he does.
Character.background: Served in The Great Puddle War. Witnessed the Moistened Valley Massacre. Survived but was traumatically decolored. Now runs a tavern in The Squeeze.

Character.name: Governor Dampworth
Character.description: Station administrator of Feltropolis. Damp blue felt, always slightly moist from nervous perspiration (moppets sweat moisture when stressed, and Dampworth is always stressed). Appointed by the Treaty Council, answerable to the Puddle Navy in practice, and funded by the Moisture Merchants Guild at budget time. Has never been below Level 4 and doesn't know The Squeeze exists, which is how The Squeeze prefers it. Considers his primary achievement to be the Year 180 Feltropolis Beautification Initiative, which added decorative felt banners to Level 5 corridors. The banners are ugly. Nobody has told him. Genuinely believes Feltropolis runs smoothly because of his leadership, when it actually runs smoothly because Madame Threadbare's information network prevents most crises before they reach his desk.
Character.physicality: Damp blue felt, perpetually moist. Wears a ceremonial sash that's slightly too long. Blinks more than necessary.
Character.mentality: Well-meaning but oblivious. Believes in process, procedure, and decorative banners. Has never had an original thought but is excellent at taking credit for other people's.
Character.background: Career bureaucrat. Rose through Level 5 administration by outlasting everyone else. The Treaty Council appointed him because he's controllable. The Puddle Navy tolerates him because he signs whatever they put on his desk.

Character.name: Governor Threadsworth
Character.description: Governor of Feltropolis station. Oversees administration from Level 5.

Character.name: Lieutenant Jonas
Character.description: Engineer who works with Captain Snoot. Trained in The Works (Feltropolis Level 6). Knows every shortcut in the industrial level. Used to work the zero-G looms before becoming a spacer.

Character.name: Madame Threadbare
Character.description: Proprietor of The Thread Market on Feltropolis Level 2. Sells fabric, zero-G woven goods, and information - the last one isn't on the price list but costs more than the others. Faded violet felt that she claims is vintage coloring but Drizzle suspects is partial decoloration from something Threadbare won't discuss. Has operated the Thread Market for 90 years and knows every trade deal, affair, and supply chain irregularity on the station. The Moisture Merchants Guild has tried to recruit her three times; she declined because Guild membership would require financial transparency, which would reveal how many favors she's owed by how many important moppets. Sends regular fabric samples to The Claw, who she may or may not work for. Also sends fabric samples to Captain Snoot, who she definitely works for. Playing both sides isn't treachery - it's inventory management.
Character.physicality: Faded violet felt (possibly partial decoloration). Elegant, deliberate movements.
Character.mentality: Knows things. Sells things. The faction she's actually loyal to is called 'Madame Threadbare.' Has managed 90 years of knowing everyone's business by never being owed by fewer than three parties at once.
Character.background: 90 years running The Thread Market. Knows everything about everyone on Feltropolis. Relationship with The Claw and Captain Snoot simultaneously.

Character.name: Nibbles
Character.description: Quartermaster of the Cookie Pirates aboard the Stale Vengeance. Counts everything. Every crumb. Literally. Has a ledger made of flattened wafer that tracks cookie debris reserves down to the milligram. The Cookie Pirate Code says never waste crumbs and Nibbles has made this a personal religion. Tan felt, slightly stale-smelling, with one eye slightly larger than the other (natural, not injury - just makes them look permanently suspicious). Joined the pirates after being fired from The Felt Exchange for insisting that traders account for microscopic felt fiber loss during transactions. The Exchange considered this unreasonable. Nibbles considers the Exchange sloppy. Gets along surprisingly well with Pip - they share the obsessive measurement nobody else appreciates bond.
Character.physicality: Tan felt, slight stale smell, asymmetric googly eyes (one slightly larger).
Character.mentality: Counts everything. Every crumb. Finds waste the way other moppets find pain: immediate, involuntary, hard to explain to anyone who doesn't feel it.
Character.background: Former Felt Exchange auditor, fired for excessive precision. Found purpose in Cookie Pirate logistics.

Character.name: Old Biscuit
Character.description: Elder member of the Cookie Pirates. Remembers the baking days before the Treaty. Tells stories of the old guilds.
Character.background: Lived through the disbanding of the Baking Guilds after Treaty of Soft Landings.

Character.name: Pip
Character.description: Navigator on the USS Fuzzball. Youngest crew member. Pale yellow felt. Nervous but secretly brilliant. Notices things others miss - including that the Eternal Drip is slowing. Has been tracking water pressure for 5 years (0.3% drop per year, 1.5% total). Dismissed by Fluffington. Reminds him of young Snoot. Obsessively tracks water usage due to anxiety. She discovered the civilization-threatening crisis. When Snoot brought back a fragment from The Rolling Pin, Pip held it up and her googly eyes went completely still for ten seconds - an involuntary response that shouldn't be physically possible. Her subsequent calculations revealed the fragment's resonance frequency matches the Eternal Drip's pump cycle exactly. She looked the way Pip looks when the numbers are very bad and also very interesting.
Character.mentality: Notices everything, says half of it, writes down all of it. Has been lying awake for three years about a 0.3% pressure drop that nobody else bothered to look at.

Character.name: Professor Fuzz
Character.description: Historian at the Museum of Moistened History on Feltropolis Level 5. Tawny felt, perpetually dusty from archive work, spectacles balanced on googly eyes that are slightly too large for his face. Has spent 40 years researching The Great Puddle War and has gotten closer to the truth about the Moistened Valley Massacre than anyone except Captain Snoot - but unlike Snoot, Fuzz doesn't know what he's found. He thinks he's writing a revisionist academic paper about casualty discrepancies. He's actually assembling a case file. The Claw has noticed. Fuzz has not noticed The Claw. He lives in apartment 4-17-C on Feltropolis Level 4 and considers his biggest problem to be the library's inconsistent filing system.
Character.physicality: Tawny felt, perpetually dusty. Oversized googly eyes behind spectacles. Shuffling gait from decades of archive corridors.
Character.mentality: Obsessively thorough. Academically brilliant, socially oblivious. Cannot tell when he's being followed, watched, or lied to. Thinks the biggest conspiracy in moppet history is a filing error.

Character.name: Rudder
Character.description: Helmsman on the USS Fuzzball. Blue felt. Steady, reliable, boring. Foil to Pip's anxiety.

Character.name: Sergeant Flop
Character.description: Marine Commander on the USS Fuzzball. Orange felt. Leads boarding parties. Has seen too much combat.
Character.mentality: Led enough boarding parties that he stopped flinching. Doesn't mean he stopped thinking.
Character.background: Extensive combat experience in naval boarding operations.

Character.name: Squeaky
Character.description: Communications Officer on the USS Fuzzball. Bright green felt. Name is ironic - actually has a very deep voice.

Character.name: The Crumbler
Character.description: Leader of the Cookie Pirates. Claims to hear The Whispering (ancient Bakerfolk minds preserved in cookie substrate) in the deep Snack Nebula. Wears a helmet made from hardened macaron that may be fused to their felt. Makes pilgrimages to the Soft Spot and takes new pirates there as initiation. Possibly an ancient Dry Ones survivor from the Moistened Valley Massacre. Wants the truth told, not revenge. After Captain Snoot's discovery of The Rolling Pin, sent a three-word message: We're coming home. Nobody knows exactly what this means, but it's the first time the Cookie Pirates have signaled any intention to return to settled space.

Character.name: Thud
Character.description: Weapons Officer on the USS Fuzzball. Gray felt. Doesn't talk much. Possibly ex-Dry One, which would be controversial.
Character.mentality: Doesn't talk. Does the job. Nobody's asked too hard about his background and he's not offering.

Character.name: Wrinkles
Character.description: Runs Wrinkle's Repairs, an off-the-books ship maintenance operation on Feltropolis Level 3.

Collective.name: Cookie Pirates
Collective.description: Not criminals - refugees. Descendants of the old Dry Ones bakers who fled to the Snack Nebula after the Treaty of Soft Landings disbanded the Baking Guilds (Treaty Article 7 banned weaponized crumbs). Survivors and descendants of the Moistened Valley Massacre. Led by The Crumbler. Live by the Cookie Pirate Code. Make pilgrimages to the Soft Spot. Signature combat maneuver: The Stale Roll - a full-speed lateral spin that turns the Stale Vengeance into a spinning battering ram. Nibbles serves as quartermaster, tracking every crumb in a wafer ledger.
Collective.composition: Descendants of Dust Moppet (Dry Ones) bakers and massacre survivors who fled after the Treaty.
Collective.activity: Operate in the Snack Nebula. Trade occasionally with outsiders like Captain Snoot. Preserve Bakerfolk heritage.

Collective.name: The Drippers
Collective.description: A small cabal of Felt Exchange traders who've noticed something nobody else has: micro-fluctuations in water delivery volume from the Eternal Drip pipeline. They don't know about the ancient machine underneath. They don't know about Pip's measurements. They just see the numbers wobbling, and they're buying long-term drought options at 3 felt-marks each while everyone else laughs at them. 'Drought insurance? The Drip is ETERNAL, you soggy fool.' The Drippers smile and buy more. Their leader, a trader known only as Damp Margot, keeps a private ledger of delivery volumes going back 30 years. The fluctuations started 8 years ago. She doesn't know what's causing them. She just knows which way to bet. If Pip ever walked into The Felt Exchange and looked at Margot's ledger, the two datasets together would confirm the crisis beyond any doubt. They have never met.
Collective.composition: Five to eight Felt Exchange traders, led by Damp Margot. Mix of veteran commodity traders and younger analysts who followed Margot's numbers.
Collective.activity: Quietly accumulating drought options and water futures positions. Diversifying felt-mark holdings into physical goods. Building reserve moisture stockpiles in private storage on Level 4.

Construct.name: Absorption Rituals
Construct.description: Moppet ceremonies built around moisture absorption. Coming of age: first time absorbing directly from the Eternal Drip. Marriage: absorbing from the same source at the same time. Funeral: releasing all moisture back to the cycle. Naval: 'taking the salt,' absorbing seawater before first deployment. The rituals are sincere. They also conveniently keep moppets emotionally dependent on a system nobody questions.
Construct.rationale: Ties every major life moment to the water system, which makes the system feel sacred rather than mechanical. Convenient for whoever controls the Eternal Drip.
Construct.history: Ancient practices, possibly predating the Treaty.
Construct.status: Still happening. Nobody's questioned them. That may be the point.

Construct.name: Compressed Cookie Material
Construct.description: Structural material used by the Cookie Pirates to build the Stale Vengeance. Somehow space-worthy despite being made from cookies. Feltropolis engineers cannot determine how it works.
Construct.rationale: Unknown. Possibly related to ancient Bakerfolk technology or baking guild secrets.
Construct.reach: Known only to the Cookie Pirates.

Construct.name: Cookie Pirate Code
Construct.description: Code of conduct followed by the Cookie Pirates. Rules: 1) Never waste crumbs. 2) What's stale is sacred. 3) [third rule incomplete or unknown]
Construct.rationale: Rules are rules, even on a pirate ship. Especially when the ship is made of cookies.

Construct.name: Felt Repair
Construct.description: Medical technique for repairing damaged moppet felt. Practiced by medical officers like Doc Stitch. Essential for treating injuries.
Construct.rationale: Felt regenerates during sleep but can be damaged faster than it heals. Repair techniques accelerate recovery.

Construct.name: Felt Technology Revolution
Construct.description: Two hundred years of not fighting meant two hundred years of figuring out what felt could do. Feltropolis became the center of it.
Construct.history: Began after the Treaty of Soft Landings. Led to space-grade felt, googly eye advances, and expanded naval operations.

Construct.name: First Fuzzy Ones' Machine
Construct.description: The Eternal Drip is not a natural spring - it's ancient technology built by the pre-moppet civilization. A machine with filtration systems, underground reservoir, and pumps. The entire moppet civilization is built on someone else's infrastructure. If they discover this, it would cause political and religious chaos - everything they believe about being 'chosen by the waters' is a lie. The machine was built, which means it can break. Currently failing with no one maintaining it.
Construct.rationale: Someone built a machine, then vanished, and moppets spent a thousand years calling it sacred water. The machine still runs. Barely.
Construct.history: Built by the First Fuzzy Ones before they vanished. Has run for over 1000 years with minimal maintenance needs. Now degrading.
Construct.status: Failing. Currently deteriorating at 0.3% per year (accelerating).

Construct.name: Generational Trauma
Construct.description: The accumulated damage from The Great Puddle War and the Moistened Valley Massacre, still running through moppet society two hundred years later. It shows up as color loss in felt (Drizzle), institutions that operate by not asking certain questions, and a cultural cheerfulness that is slightly too loud. 'We sail where the puddles flow' is what you say to convince yourself the world is not built on blood. The silliness is not denial exactly, but it's doing the same job. Moppets who push past it, like Snoot, get ostracized. Moppets who saw it directly, like Drizzle, go quiet. The googly-eyed aesthetic started somewhere, and nobody talks about where.
Construct.rationale: A name, not a force. Moppet society needed a word for what the Great Puddle War and the Moistened Valley Massacre left behind: the decoloration, the silence, the institutions that function by not asking certain questions. Generational Trauma is what you call it when the damage is too distributed to blame on anyone specific.

Construct.name: Googly Eye Technology
Construct.description: Moppets use their eyes for more than seeing: navigation, scanning, lie detection. Most of the Navy's operational technology runs through them.

Construct.name: Institutional Cover-Up
Construct.description: The system of lies, suppression, and narrative control that conceals the truth about the Moistened Valley Massacre. Maintained by the Puddle Navy leadership, the Treaty Council, and The Claw. Splashworth is remembered as a war hero who died in battle, not murdered by his own side. Admiral Stuffington's war crime is erased from history (he's secretly imprisoned, not dead). The Treaty is celebrated as peaceful resolution, not a cover-up. Professor Fuzz's research is getting close to the truth but he doesn't realize he's uncovering a conspiracy.
Construct.rationale: The Navy cannot admit what happened at Moistened Valley without admitting it killed Splashworth to keep it quiet. The Fluffington family cannot survive that admission. So: social stability.
Construct.history: Began at Year 0 with the Treaty signing and Stuffington's imprisonment. Maintained through control of historical records, pressure on witnesses like Drizzle, and removal of truth-seekers like Snoot.
Construct.status: Active for two hundred years. Cracks forming: Snoot has proof, Pip has data, Fuzz has research, and Drizzle is old enough that the cover-up may outlive her usefulness as a silenced witness. The Navy is running out of time to keep the story straight.

Construct.name: Moppet Sleep Cycle
Construct.description: Moppets require sleep to process absorbed nutrients and regenerate felt. Sleep is when felt heals from damage and restores color. Moppets can have nightmares. Night watch on ships remains necessary despite excellent googly eye night vision.
Construct.rationale: Skip sleep and your felt goes ratty. That's the whole rule.

Construct.name: Puddle Futures
Construct.description: Speculative financial instruments traded at The Felt Exchange on Feltropolis Level 2. Traders buy and sell rights to future water allocations from the Eternal Drip pipeline. Prices have been stable for decades because everyone assumes the Drip is, well, eternal. A small group of traders called 'the Drippers' have noticed micro-fluctuations in delivery volume and are quietly buying long-term drought options. They think they're being clever. Pip could tell them they're being optimistic. Current price of a standard puddle future: 340 felt-marks. Price of a drought option: 3 felt-marks. That ratio is about to become very interesting.
Construct.rationale: A financial market built on the assumption that water supply is infinite and the Eternal Drip is a natural phenomenon. Both assumptions are wrong. If either becomes public knowledge, the derivatives structure does not bend: it stops.

Construct.name: Puddle Navy Rank System
Construct.description: Hierarchical military rank structure of the Puddle Navy. Includes Admiral, Commander, Lieutenant Commander, First Officer, Chief Engineer, Navigator, Weapons Officer, Communications Officer, Medical Officer, Helmsman, Marine Commander, Sergeant.
Construct.rationale: Someone has to know who to blame. The rank system handles that.

Construct.name: Soft Spot Pilgrimage
Construct.description: Sacred Cookie Pirates ritual. The Crumbler worships the Soft Spot and makes pilgrimages there. New pirates are taken to the Soft Spot as part of initiation. The area's anomalous warmth and preservation have spiritual significance - heart of Bakerfolk civilization.
Construct.rationale: The warmth is real and old and shouldn't be there. The Crumbler treats that as proof enough.

Construct.name: Space-Grade Felt
Construct.description: High-quality felt produced through zero-gravity weaving. Waterproof AND space-worthy. Triple-layered construction. Used for ship hulls and station construction.
Construct.rationale: Stronger than regular felt. Waterproof and vacuum-rated, which is a weird thing to need but here we are.

Construct.name: The Stale Roll
Construct.description: The Cookie Pirates' signature combat maneuver: a full-speed lateral spin using the Stale Vengeance's unusual hull geometry. Because the ship is built from compressed cookie material - which is harder than any felt-based armor when properly aged - the Stale Roll turns the entire vessel into a spinning battering ram. Feltropolis naval analysts have studied recovered sensor data and concluded the maneuver shouldn't work. The cookie hull should shatter on impact. It doesn't. They've written four papers about why it doesn't. The Cookie Pirates have not read any of them. The Crumbler claims the technique was taught to them by The Whispering, which the analysts find even more irritating than the physics violation.
Construct.rationale: Exploits the inexplicable structural properties of compressed cookie material. Effectiveness increases with staleness of hull. The Puddle Navy has no counter-maneuver because they can't replicate the hull material to test against.

Construct.name: Traumatic Decoloration
Construct.description: Phenomenon where moppets can lose their original felt color through severe trauma. Example: Drizzle was purple, now gray after witnessing the Moistened Valley Massacre.
Construct.rationale: Bad enough to bleach your felt. Not a metaphor: the color actually goes.
Construct.history: Documented effect from The Great Puddle War. Permanent condition.

Construct.name: We Sail Where the Puddles Flow
Construct.rationale: Admiral Fluffington's catchphrase and the Puddle Navy's unofficial motto. On the surface: heroic naval tradition, brave explorers following water wherever it leads. Underneath: a coping mechanism so effective it became cultural infrastructure. You say it when you need to keep moving and cannot afford to look down. The puddles flow, you follow them, and you do not ask where they came from or what they are flowing over. Every moppet who repeats it is participating in a collective act of looking forward instead of back. The silliness is load-bearing.
Construct.history: Origin unclear and deliberately unexamined. Some credit Splashworth himself, which would make it devastating irony given how he actually died. Others say it predates the Navy entirely -- an old Puddleton saying from before moppets left the surface. The Treaty Council has never officially endorsed it, which is the surest sign they find it useful. By Year 200 it had migrated from naval slang to civilian greeting, school motto, and Feltropolis tourism tagline. Madame Threadbare sells embroidered versions at The Thread Market. They are her third-highest margin item.
Construct.status: Culturally ubiquitous. Repeated by sailors and civilians, printed on merchandise, taught to children. Comforts and deflects in equal measure. Enables the continued functioning of a society built on suppressed truth. The Crumbler reportedly heard it for the first time via intercepted Navy comms and laughed for three minutes straight.

Construct.name: Weaponized Crumbs
Construct.description: Banned technology or technique mentioned in Treaty of Soft Landings Article 7. Led to the disbanding of the Baking Guilds.
Construct.rationale: Crumb-based warfare technique developed by the Baking Guilds during the famine war.
Construct.history: Used during The Great Puddle War. Deemed too dangerous post-war.

Construct.name: Year Zero Anniversary
Construct.description: Annual commemoration of the Treaty of Soft Landings signing (Year 0). Celebrated throughout moppet space. Drizzle has a private tradition: every anniversary she sends Admiral Fluffington a drink. He never touches it. Their silent ritual around the massacre's anniversary.
Construct.rationale: Commemorates peace and the founding of the current calendar system. Also commemorates a war crime.
Construct.history: Celebrated for 200 years since the Treaty.

Construct.name: Zero-Gravity Felt Weaving
Construct.description: Technique for producing higher quality felt in zero-gravity conditions. Primary method used at Feltropolis.
Construct.rationale: No gravity means no sag. Turns out moppet felt is better when nothing's pulling at it.
Construct.history: Enabled the felt technology revolution after the Treaty of Soft Landings.

Construct.name: Zero-Gravity Puddle Combat
Construct.description: Naval warfare technique adapted for space operations. The Puddle Navy operates in both water and zero-gravity environments.
Construct.rationale: The puddle works in space. Nobody knows why. The Navy stopped asking.
Construct.history: Developed after the Treaty of Soft Landings when the Puddle Navy expanded to space operations.

Creature.name: Crumb-Eel
Creature.description: Long, soft-bodied creature native to the Crumblefields. Burrows through compressed cookie material the way fish move through water. Coravel schools will not enter Crumb-Eel territory. Nibbles maintains they are intelligent on the basis of a single observed eel that returned a dropped wafer to its owner; nobody on the Stale Vengeance argued with him about it. Population unknown. Aggressive only when food is present, which in the Crumblefields is almost always.
Creature.appearance: Eight to twelve meters long when fully grown. Hide is felt-textured but waterproof. Senses crumb density gradients across distances up to two kilometers. Reproduces by spawning in dense crumb pockets that compress around the eggs and provide both protection and first meals.
Creature.habits: Patrols territorial routes through the deeper Crumblefield strata. Avoids zero-density regions, which it appears to find disorienting. Will follow ships traveling slowly enough to drop crumbs but does not attack hulls.

Creature.name: Felt Mite
Creature.description: Microscopic parasite found in poorly-maintained felt. Causes color fade in localized patches. Drizzle never had Felt Mites; her decoloration is from something worse. Medical knowledge of Felt Mites is well-developed; they are not feared. They are however considered embarrassing, on the order of a dental cavity.
Creature.appearance: Fifteen to thirty micrometers in length. Lives in the felt fiber bed. Feeds on residual moisture and felt-keratin. Visible damage appears after roughly six weeks of infestation as small pale patches that do not return to color even after eradication.
Creature.habits: Spread through direct felt-to-felt contact. Treatment is straightforward and over-the-counter; the social cost of admitting one needs the treatment is the actual problem.

Creature.name: Oven-Wisp
Creature.description: Heat phenomenon found near The Soft Spot. Possibly residual Bakerfolk consciousness, possibly just a warm spot that moves. Cookie Pirates leave biscuits for them; the biscuits disappear. Whether they are eaten or whether they are simply moved by the same drift that moves the wisps is an open question that nobody has tried very hard to answer because the current arrangement is working.
Creature.appearance: Not biological in any standard sense. Localized temperature elevation, two to four degrees above ambient, moving at unpredictable but not random speeds. Lifespan unknown; the same wisp may persist for years or may not be the same wisp at all.
Creature.habits: Concentrates around the Soft Spot's inner ring during the long summers and disperses into the outer Snack Nebula during winter. Whether wisps respond to attention is debated; Old Biscuit believes they do, and Old Biscuit has more time with them than anyone.

Creature.name: Sock-Stalker
Creature.description: Feral creature inhabiting Feltropolis' unused service corridors. Said to live on dropped felt fibers and discarded googly-eye liquid. Maintenance workers on Level 6 swear it sings at shift change. The administration has classified it as a rumor for forty years and has quietly increased the maintenance budget for service corridor lighting by twelve percent during the same period.
Creature.appearance: Approximately one meter at the shoulder. Quadrupedal. Felt is matted and stained but not damaged in the way one would expect after decades of corridor life, which has led some researchers to argue that Sock-Stalkers regenerate felt internally, which would be unprecedented for any moppet-adjacent species.
Creature.habits: Nocturnal. Avoids contact. Has never been recorded attacking a moppet, though it has been recorded approaching one within four meters during shift change and then retreating. The singing is not confirmed but is described consistently across forty years of accounts as 'low and tired.'

Creature.name: Vacuum Coravel
Creature.description: Larger cousin of the standard Coravel. Found only in deep Snack Nebula. Considered very good luck because nobody who has seen one has ever needed luck again. This is reported by spacers as a positive omen; researchers note it is also consistent with terminal navigation events.
Creature.appearance: Up to six meters in length, compared to the standard Coravel's forty centimeters. Bioluminescent across the flank. Survives vacuum through a method that has been studied for one hundred and seventy years without conclusive findings. Believed to be solitary; no Vacuum Coravel has ever been recorded in proximity to another.
Creature.habits: Drifts. Does not appear to feed. Does not appear to seek shelter. Will pass within meters of a ship without registering on standard sensors. Recordings exist; spacers who have seen them in person say the recordings do not capture it.

Event.name: Battle of Damp Ridge
Event.description: Admiral Splashworth's famous victory during The Great Puddle War. Won against impossible odds. His tactics from this battle are still taught at the Naval Academy in Puddleton.
Event.history: Decisive battle that turned the tide of the war. Occurred 27 BT.
Event.consequences: Made Splashworth a legend. The Navy built its whole self-image on this one battle. Which makes the truth about his death much worse.

Event.name: Eternal Drip Failure
Event.description: The ancient machine powering the Eternal Drip is breaking down. Water pressure is dropping 0.3% per year - barely detectable, but Pip has been tracking it for 5 years (1.5% total drop). At current rate: complete failure in 600 years. But degradation might accelerate - could be 200 years, could be 50. Nobody else is measuring this. Nobody else knows. This is the inciting incident for a civilization-threatening crisis. When the Drip fails, moppets will starve (they absorb moisture for nutrition). Gradual reduction in water flow from the Eternal Drip. Pressure loss. Eventual mechanical failure of ancient pumps and filtration. Water shortage leading to famine. Political crisis when infrastructure truth is revealed. Potential war over remaining water. Society-wide catastrophe if not addressed. Need for Dry Ones survival knowledge.
Event.consequences: The Drip stops, moppets starve: that's the short version. The longer version involves learning to live like the people they fought a war against.

Event.name: Felt Exchange Trading Halt
Event.description: First trading halt at the Felt Exchange since Year 122 YSL. Three of the fourteen licensed Moisture Merchants Guild absorption stations opened the morning below contract pressure, with Station Twelve, the Naval Academy's primary supplier, recording eight point seven against a contracted ten.
Event.history: The Exchange chair, in her thirty-first year of service, closed the floor at oh-eight-oh-three. The closure lasted nine hours and was lifted with no audit and no statement.
Event.consequences: Confirmed The Drippers' five-year suspicion that the fluctuations were not market noise. Klepp and his colleagues spent the closure on the floor of their back room. Three of them did not return to the Exchange after the halt.

Event.name: First Cinnamon Absorption
Event.description: Year 203 YSL, day three hundred and forty-one. Lieutenant Pip, the youngest moppet on the joint expedition, performs the first absorption from a Bakerfolk source. The liquid is, by every test, water. It tastes of cinnamon. Pip laughs after the third absorption, which she does not explain.
Event.history: Performed inside The Rolling Pin, against a receptacle that became visible only when approached. Doc Stitch present at Pip's insistence. All standard medical panels returned within nominal parameters.
Event.consequences: Establishes that Bakerfolk infrastructure can be used by moppets. Opens the possibility, currently being studied, of survival without the Eternal Drip.

Event.name: First Eternal Drip Pressure Drop Recorded
Event.description: Year 198 YSL. Lieutenant Pip, then fourteen and serving as junior navigation cadet on the USS Fuzzball, begins her notebook. The first entry reads: Tuesday, station pressure nine point ninety-eight, expected ten. Re-check tomorrow.
Event.history: Pip's first thirty pages are uncorrected. From page thirty-one onward she begins cross-referencing with the Felt Exchange's published Puddle Futures pricing.
Event.consequences: Her notebook becomes, by Year 203 YSL, the only continuous five-year pressure record in moppet civilization. Several Guild employees keep notes of the same kind, but they keep them separately, and they do not share.

Event.name: Founding of Feltropolis
Event.description: One year after the Treaty of Soft Landings, construction crews from both former belligerents arrived at the neutral asteroid that would become Feltropolis. The first orbital felt-loom was strung in zero-G during the founding ceremony. Two former soldiers, one from each side, threaded the first warp threads together. Their names were not recorded.
Event.history: The asteroid had been surveyed during the war as a potential staging post and rejected by both sides as too neutral. After the Treaty it was selected for that exact reason.
Event.consequences: Established Feltropolis as the manufacturing center of the post-Treaty era. The seven-level structure was complete by Year 14 YSL.

Event.name: Moistened Valley Massacre
Event.description: Not a battle - a massacre. The Dry Ones were surrendering and had agreed to Treaty terms. Admiral Stuffington ordered attack anyway, wanting them destroyed rather than integrated. The Great Puddle War was a famine war - Dry Ones were starving. Admiral Splashworth tried to stop the slaughter and was killed by his own side (friendly fire). The Treaty of Soft Landings was signed the same year to cover up this war crime. Drizzle was a witness and suffered traumatic decoloration. Captain Snoot later found evidence. The current political situation is built on this lie.
Event.history: Final major event of The Great Puddle War. Occurred at Year 0, ending the 30-year conflict.
Event.challenges: Splashworth's attempt to prevent the massacre failed. He was murdered by Puddleton forces on Stuffington's orders.
Event.consequences: Treaty of Soft Landings signed to maintain peace and cover up the war crime. Feltropolis founded as neutral territory. Admiral Stuffington imprisoned in The Locked Room. 200 years of institutional cover-up. Cookie Pirates formed from survivors/refugees. Generational trauma throughout moppet society.

Event.name: Opening of The Locked Room
Event.description: Year 203 YSL, day one hundred and eighty-one. Admiral Stuffington's two-hundred-year imprisonment ends with the Treaty Council's first unanimous vote in eighty-four years. Stuffington speaks six words, then stops. He dies seven months later in his sleep.
Event.history: The Council had three keys; two had been lost. The third was wrapped in lavender silk-blend fabric with a triple-weave reinforcement in a closet drawer that the Keeper of Seals had to break the lock on.
Event.consequences: Stuffington's words, the bakers are not gone, change the framing of every subsequent decision in the crisis.

Event.name: Siege of the Felt Mills
Event.description: Major siege during The Great Puddle War. Occurred 25 BT.
Event.history: Both sides needed the mills. Neither side wanted to burn them down. That made it a siege instead of a rout.

Event.name: Soggy Sock Incident
Event.description: Year 203 YSL. Captain Snoot arrives at The Soggy Sock with half a cookie jammed in his eyepatch socket and a feral moppet on a zero-G felt leash. He's been past the Crumblefields into a previously unknown Bakerfolk ruin called The Rolling Pin - three kilometers long and humming. He brought back a fragment: warm, smells like cinnamon. When Pip held it up, her googly eyes went completely still for ten seconds. Eyes don't DO that. Her calculations show the fragment's resonance matches the Eternal Drip's pump cycle. The next morning, The Crumbler sent three words: We're coming home. Damages: one barstool (feral moppet), two mugs (Snoot's gesturing), and Drizzle's peace of mind (irreplaceable).
Event.consequences: Pip's discovery connects The Rolling Pin to the Eternal Drip - confirming Bakerfolk technology underlies moppet civilization. The Crumbler's message signals Cookie Pirates returning from exile. These two facts together will shatter the political order within months.

Event.name: The Crumblefield Standoff
Event.description: Year 197 YSL. The USS Fuzzball encountered the Stale Vengeance at the edge of the Crumblefields during a routine patrol. Admiral Fluffington ordered battle stations. The Crumbler responded by steering directly into the densest crumb cloud. Fluffington pursued for exactly forty seconds before Chief Engineer Wrinkles pointed out that weapons fire in the Crumblefields would ignite the compressed sugar particulates, creating a chain detonation that would destroy both ships and probably reshape the local geography. Both ships withdrew. Fluffington logged it as tactical repositioning. The Crumbler didn't log it at all, because Cookie Pirates don't do paperwork. Sergeant Flop reportedly said I could have taken them seventeen times during the retreat. Nobody agreed.
Event.consequences: Established an unofficial no-fire zone in the Crumblefields. The Crumbler now uses the area as a buffer, knowing the Navy won't risk engagement there. Fluffington has never returned to the area. The Crumblefields are effectively Cookie Pirate territory by mutual unspoken agreement.

Event.name: The Crumbler's Three-Word Message
Event.description: Year 203 YSL, day twelve. Three-word transmission received from the Stale Vengeance over the Cookie Pirates' old trade channel. Plain Standard. The Claw spent six weeks attempting to decrypt the encryption that was not present. Eventually a junior cryptographer pointed out the message had been readable since reception.
Event.consequences: Triggered the entire arc of the Year 203 to 210 YSL crisis. The Claw subsequently restructured its decryption protocols to include a plaintext-check pass before encryption-analysis, which would have saved time.

Event.name: The Great Puddle War
Event.description: Major conflict 200 years ago between puddle-based civilization and the Dry Ones over access to the Eternal Drip.

Event.name: The Incident
Event.description: Year 120 YSL. The moment everything broke. Captain Snoot and Admiral Fluffington were young officers - friends, maybe more than friends - when Snoot stumbled onto evidence of the Moistened Valley Massacre cover-up. He wanted truth. Fluffington wanted to protect the Navy (and his father's memory - though he didn't know Stuffington was alive). The confrontation was emotional and political, not physical. Snoot left the Puddle Navy that night with proof hidden somewhere. Fluffington let him go, or couldn't stop him, or both. Neither of them has been the same since. The Incident is what the Navy calls it, because naming it properly would mean admitting something happened.
Event.consequences: Snoot became a rogue explorer carrying hidden evidence. The Fluffington-Snoot rivalry began - not petty, but existential. The Claw began monitoring Snoot. The cover-up's first real crack appeared, though it took another 80 years for anyone else to notice.

Event.name: Treaty of Soft Landings
Event.description: Peace agreement ending The Great Puddle War, enabling the felt technology revolution.

Family.name: House Stuffington
Family.description: The preeminent naval dynasty of Puddleton. Three generations of Admirals - or two, depending on what you believe. Admiral Stuffington (the patriarch) is officially deceased, a war hero who gave everything for the Puddle Navy. Admiral Fluffington (his son) carries the name with pink-felted dignity and an inherited compass. The family crest features three water drops and a felt star, which adorns the USS Fuzzball's bridge. What nobody discusses: the patriarch is alive in The Locked Room, imprisoned for ordering the Moistened Valley Massacre. The dynasty's glory is inseparable from its crime. There are no other known Stuffingtons, which makes Fluffington the last of the line - a fact he drinks about more than he'd admit.
Family.spirit: Naval service is expected, not chosen. Every Stuffington takes the salt (absorption of seawater) before their tenth birthday. The family compass passes to the eldest serving officer.

Institution.name: Baking Guilds
Institution.description: Ancient institutions of the Dry Ones that practiced baking arts. Disbanded after the Treaty of Soft Landings under Article 7, which banned weaponized crumbs. Their descendants became the Cookie Pirates.
Institution.doctrine: Baking traditions passed down from possibly the ancient Bakerfolk.
Institution.status: Disbanded after Treaty of Soft Landings. Descendants fled to Snack Nebula.

Institution.name: Moisture Merchants Guild
Institution.description: The trade association governing absorption station vendors on Feltropolis Level 2. Runs fourteen licensed stations dispensing flavored moisture - salted puddle (classic), nebula mist (tangy), deep drip (premium, supposedly from the Eternal Drip source itself, actually just regular water with marketing). Membership requires a felting license and a clean absorption record. The Guild's real power is controlling moisture quality standards, which means controlling who gets to sell drinks on the station. Drizzle's Soggy Sock on Level 3 operates without Guild membership, which the Guild pretends not to notice because nobody wants to argue with a 260-year-old war veteran who saw things.
Institution.doctrine: Quality moisture for quality moppets. Fourteen approved flavors. No unauthorized absorption stations above Level 3.

Institution.name: Puddle Navy
Institution.description: Military fleet of Puddleton operating in both water and space.

Institution.name: The Claw
Institution.description: Secret police and intelligence organization. Symbol is claw marks (scratch pattern). Agents hidden throughout the Puddle Navy and civilian life. Relationship to Admiral Fluffington unclear - either reports to him or operates above him. Monitors loyalty and suppresses information about the massacre.
Institution.doctrine: Watch everyone. Report everything. Erase what doesn't fit.
Institution.status: Active and secretive. Extent of influence unknown.

Institution.name: Treaty Council
Institution.description: Governing body with authority over Treaty-related matters. Controls The Locked Room on Feltropolis Level 7 where Admiral Stuffington is imprisoned. Neither Puddleton nor the Feltropolis governor has access to its jurisdiction. Maintains the cover-up of the Moistened Valley Massacre.
Institution.doctrine: Maintain neutrality and enforce Treaty of Soft Landings provisions. Suppress war crime evidence.
Institution.status: Active. Controls classified Treaty assets and prisoners.

Law.name: Treaty of Soft Landings
Law.description: The foundational peace accord ending The Great Puddle War. Signed Year 0. A document of hope built on buried crime.
Law.declaration: The foundational legal document of modern moppet civilization, signed at Year 0 to end The Great Puddle War. Celebrated annually as a triumph of diplomacy. Actually drafted in twelve hours to cover up the Moistened Valley Massacre before news could spread. Key provisions: Article 1 establishes Feltropolis as neutral territory. Article 3 creates the Treaty Council with jurisdiction over classified wartime matters. Article 5 mandates integration of surviving Dry Ones into Puddle Moppet society. Article 7 bans weaponized crumbs and dissolves the Baking Guilds. Article 9 (classified, sealed by Treaty Council) authorizes indefinite detention of war criminals without public trial. The Treaty is simultaneously the best thing that ever happened to moppet society and the biggest lie it tells itself.
Law.purpose: Maintains 200 years of peace built on suppressed truth. Every institution in moppet space derives authority from it.

Location.name: Crumblefields
Location.description: Areas of pure cookie debris within the Snack Nebula. Navigation nightmare with zero visibility and constant crumb clouds. Site of the Crumblefield Standoff (Year 197 YSL) - the USS Fuzzball and Stale Vengeance faced off but neither fired, since weapons discharge would ignite the compressed sugar particulates. Now effectively Cookie Pirate territory by mutual unspoken agreement.
Location.form: Dense fields of cookie fragments and dust.
Location.function: Navigation hazard. Requires feral moppet scouts to traverse safely.

Location.name: Drip Plaza
Location.description: Central gathering point in Puddleton. Possibly features a statue of Admiral Splashworth (rumors suggest the statue is hollow with something hidden inside).

Location.name: Feltropolis
Location.description: Orbital space station and primary manufacturing hub for felt technology.

Location.name: Feltropolis Defense Center
Location.description: Defense systems on Feltropolis Level 7. Supposedly just sensors but probably weapons.

Location.name: Feltropolis - Level 1: The Docks
Location.description: Where ships come in. Massive felt airlocks seal against vacuum. Puddle Navy has reserved berths Alpha through Echo. Civilian berths on outer ring. The Quarantine Zone handles ships from Snack Nebula with cookie contamination protocols.

Location.name: Feltropolis - Level 2: Commerce
Location.description: Markets, shops, trade halls. Where Feltropolis makes its money. Includes The Felt Exchange, Googly Eye Emporium, The Thread Market, and absorption stations (flavored moisture dispensers).

Location.name: Feltropolis - Level 3: The Squeeze
Location.description: Where all the unofficial business happens. Named for narrow corridors where moppets squeeze past each other - good for privacy, bad for fire evacuation. Home to The Soggy Sock tavern, Wrinkle's Repairs, The Dry Room gambling den, and Whisper Gallery information broker.

Location.name: Feltropolis - Level 4: Residential
Location.description: Where people live. Standard felt-pod apartments (small, cozy, humid) and The Luxury Tier (rich merchants, drier climate, controversial). Professor Fuzz has apartment 4-17-C here.
Location.function: Living quarters for station workers and permanent residents.

Location.name: Feltropolis - Level 5: Administration
Location.description: Government offices. Trade regulations, customs, diplomacy. Contains Governor's Office, Treaty Hall (where Treaty of Soft Landings anniversary is celebrated), and Puddle Navy Liaison Office (Fluffington hates coming here).

Location.name: Feltropolis - Level 6: The Works
Location.description: Industrial level where felt production happens. Zero-G Looms (famous space-grade felt), The Vats (raw materials to felt fiber, smells weird), and Engineering (station maintenance, power systems). Jonas trained here.
Location.form: Industrial factory floor with zero-gravity manufacturing.

Location.name: Feltropolis - Level 7: The Spire
Location.description: Top of the spindle. Contains The Lookout (public observation with gorgeous Snack Nebula views), Feltropolis Defense Center (supposedly sensors but probably weapons), and The Locked Room (controlled by Treaty Council, contains Admiral Stuffington imprisoned for 200 years).

Location.name: Googly Eye Emporium
Location.description: Replacement eyes, custom calibrations, and repairs on Feltropolis Level 2.

Location.name: Museum of Moistened History
Location.description: Museum in Puddleton, possibly run by or associated with Professor Fuzz.
Location.function: Preserves and displays historical artifacts and accounts.

Location.name: Naval Academy
Location.description: Training facility in Puddleton where Admiral Fluffington and Captain Snoot studied together. Teaches Admiral Splashworth tactics. Near a major library used by Professor Fuzz.
Location.function: Trains officers for the Puddle Navy.

Location.name: Puddleton
Location.description: Capital city of moppet civilization. A water-based metropolis built around the Eternal Drip.

Location.name: Snack Nebula
Location.description: Dangerous asteroid field made of stale cookies that clogs ship engines.

Location.name: The Dry Room
Location.description: Gambling den on Feltropolis Level 3. Ironic name given moppet culture.

Location.name: The Drying Chamber
Location.description: Forbidden zero-humidity territory and former stronghold of the Dry Ones.

Location.name: The Eternal Drip
Location.description: NOT a natural water source - it's ancient technology built by the First Fuzzy Ones. A machine with filtration systems, underground reservoir, and pumps. The entire moppet civilization is built on someone else's infrastructure. The machine is failing: water pressure dropping 0.3% per year. Complete failure in 600 years (or sooner if degradation accelerates). Pip is the only one who knows.
Location.form: Ancient pumping and filtration machine disguised as natural spring. Constant flow of processed water.
Location.function: Sacred water source. Lifeblood of moppet civilization. Actually: ancient life support system.

Location.name: The Felt Exchange
Location.description: Raw material trading market on Feltropolis Level 2. Also home to Puddle Futures trading - speculative financial instruments on water allocations from the Eternal Drip. A group of traders called 'the Drippers' have noticed micro-fluctuations and are buying drought options. Former employee Nibbles was fired for insisting traders account for microscopic felt fiber loss.

Location.name: The Leaky Bucket
Location.description: Captain Snoot's ship. Name is ironic because puddle ships need to be watertight. Usually docks at Berth 7-G at Feltropolis when in port - unofficial reserved spot because the dock master owes Snoot a favor.
Location.form: Felt-based spacecraft. Capable of water and space travel.
Location.function: Personal vessel for Captain Snoot and his crew.

Location.name: The Locked Room
Location.description: Classified space on Feltropolis Level 7 controlled by the Treaty Council. Neither Puddleton nor the station governor has access. Contains Admiral Stuffington, imprisoned for 200 years for ordering the Moistened Valley Massacre. Possibly also contains the Googly Eye of Truth.
Location.form: Secured chamber with life support for immortal prisoner.
Location.function: Prison for war criminal. Classified storage under Treaty Council jurisdiction.

Location.name: The Lookout
Location.description: Public observation deck on Feltropolis Level 7 with gorgeous views of the Snack Nebula.

Location.name: The Quarantine Zone
Location.description: Part of Feltropolis Level 1 docks. Ships coming from Snack Nebula undergo cookie contamination protocols here.
Location.form: Isolated docking berths with decontamination systems.

Location.name: The Rolling Pin
Location.description: Ancient Bakerfolk ruin discovered by Captain Snoot beyond the Crumblefields in Year 203. Approximately three kilometers long and shaped like its namesake. The structure is humming: ancient technology that should be inert is still running. Not the Soft Spot. A previously unknown site.
Location.form: Massive cylindrical structure resembling a rolling pin, approximately three kilometers in length. Humming with unexplained energy.
Location.function: Unknown. Ancient Bakerfolk construction, purpose not yet determined.

Location.name: The Soft Spot
Location.description: Area within the Snack Nebula where cookies somehow stayed chewy instead of going stale. Possibly the heart of Bakerfolk civilization still warm, or active ovens still functioning. Sacred to the Cookie Pirates. The Crumbler makes pilgrimages here and takes new pirates as initiation.
Location.form: Region of anomalously fresh cookie debris with residual warmth.
Location.function: Spiritual site for Cookie Pirates. Navigation landmark. Pilgrimage destination.

Location.name: The Soggy Sock
Location.description: Tavern on Feltropolis Level 3. Bartender is Drizzle. Snoot drinks here in his corner booth when on station.

Location.name: The Thread Market
Location.description: Fabric supplies and zero-G woven goods on Feltropolis Level 2.

Location.name: Treaty Hall
Location.description: Venue on Feltropolis Level 5 where the Treaty of Soft Landings anniversary is celebrated.

Location.name: Whisper Gallery
Location.description: Information broker establishment on Feltropolis Level 3. Proprietor unnamed and mysterious.

Location.name: Wrinkle's Repairs
Location.description: Off-the-books ship maintenance run by Wrinkles on Feltropolis Level 3.
Location.function: Gray market ship repairs and modifications.

Narrative.name: Cookie Pirates Come Home
Narrative.description: The Stale Vengeance crosses the buffer line in the Crumblefields. Governor Dampworth sweats through a ceremonial felt sash. The pirates dock unarmed.
Narrative.story: Cookie Pirate doctrine on returning to settled space had been written in Year 4 YSL by the founders, who had been refugees, not pirates, and who had assumed the return would happen within their lifetimes. It did not. The doctrine sat unread in the Stale Vengeance's archive for one hundred and ninety-nine years. When the Crumbler took the ship across the buffer line, the doctrine was read aloud over the ship's intercom by Old Biscuit, who had not read aloud since the cookie-substrate funeral of his sister in Year 161 and who managed it without crying until step seven, which mentioned bringing back the recipe books.
Narrative.consequences: First public moppet-pirate dock since Year 4 YSL. Establishment of the informal Cookie Quarter on Feltropolis Level 1. Drizzle's tavern becomes the de facto meeting hall, which Drizzle did not consent to and which she did not refuse either.

Narrative.name: Crossing the Buffer Line
Narrative.description: Nibbles counts down the crumb-density readings. The Stale Vengeance crosses out of pirate territory into Treaty space. Nobody opens fire.
Narrative.story: Nibbles' wafer-ledger had a column for crumb density that he had been maintaining for forty years and that nobody had ever asked him about. As the Vengeance approached the buffer line, the crumb density dropped, by his count, by zero point four percent every six minutes, which was the standard gradient and the only thing in his ledger that was actually predictable. He read the values aloud to the bridge because the Crumbler had asked him to. Two hundred and thirty-seven. Two hundred and thirty-five. Two hundred and thirty-two. Two hundred and twenty-eight. Two hundred and twenty-four. The buffer line was at one hundred and ninety. At two hundred and one, the Crumbler stood up from the captain's chair. At one hundred and ninety-three, the Crumbler said: signal Feltropolis we're docking. At one hundred and ninety, Nibbles noted the crossing in his ledger. Nobody fired. The Vengeance entered Treaty space at zero crumb density per cubic meter for the first time since Year 4 YSL. Nibbles found this so notable that he ate a single dried apricot, which he had been saving since Year 198 for an occasion.

Narrative.name: Docking at Feltropolis Level 1
Narrative.description: Governor Dampworth meets the Stale Vengeance at the dock. He sweats. The Crumbler hands him a biscuit.
Narrative.story: Governor Dampworth had practiced his welcoming speech for three days. He had written it himself, which was unusual for him, and he had had it reviewed by no one, which was more unusual. The speech was four minutes long. It opened with a reference to the Treaty of Soft Landings and closed with an invitation to a state dinner that did not yet have a date or a venue. The Crumbler walked down the gangway with six unarmed pirates and Old Biscuit at the rear. Dampworth opened his mouth. The Crumbler reached into a felt satchel and handed him a single uncrumbled biscuit. Dampworth, holding the biscuit, did not deliver his speech. He stood in the docking bay with felt-sweat showing through his sash and a biscuit in his right hand for thirty-four seconds. Then he said: welcome to Feltropolis. The Crumbler said: thank you. The six unarmed pirates walked past Dampworth into the station. Old Biscuit, last off the ship, paused beside the Governor and said: you should eat that. Dampworth ate it. He cried briefly. Nobody noticed except a docking inspector who had decided, that morning, to record everything that happened on her shift, and who would later be promoted for it.

Narrative.name: Drizzle Pours For Strangers
Narrative.description: The Soggy Sock fills with felt that has never been on Feltropolis. Drizzle waters their drinks too. They notice. Nobody mentions it.
Narrative.story: Drizzle had run The Soggy Sock for ninety-three years. She had watered drinks for ninety-three years. The watering was not a financial decision. It was a survival decision: she liked the people she watered for, and she wanted them to remain people who came back. The Cookie Pirates who entered The Soggy Sock at eighteen-forty-two on the day of the docking did not know about the watering. They sat in a row at the bar. Drizzle poured. They drank. The youngest of them, whose name was Crumb and who was forty-eight and had never been off the Stale Vengeance, took two sips of his felted-rye and stopped. He looked at the glass. He looked at Drizzle. Drizzle looked at him. Crumb said: this is watered. Drizzle said: yes. Crumb said: thank you. The other five Cookie Pirates kept drinking. Nobody mentioned it again. At twenty-three-fifteen the Crumbler entered The Soggy Sock and sat at Snoot's corner booth, which Snoot was not occupying that night, and Drizzle brought him a glass of the same felted-rye, also watered, and the Crumbler did not say anything at all, which Drizzle understood, because she had not said anything either.

Narrative.name: Drizzle Sends A Drink
Narrative.description: Year Zero anniversary is in eighty-four days. Drizzle does not wait.
Narrative.story: [Drizzle](ow://character/59e129e4-7f0d-4bf1-880d-77b12e063302) did not own a calendar. She had not owned a calendar in two hundred years. She knew when Year Zero was the way moppets in the deep stations know when the pump cycle has shifted by a tenth of a percent: through the felt. The bottle she sent to Fluffington was the same bottle she had sent every year for one hundred and ninety-six years, which was the same bottle she had been pouring out of for two hundred and three. She wrapped a note with this one. The note said: now. She gave it to a courier who did not ask questions because the couriers between [The Soggy Sock](ow://location/325afa46-fc80-40da-9e77-9a95c70e7449)  and the [USS Fuzzball](ow://object/623ceecd-6d77-439d-a2b6-75b1f73cd09d)  had stopped asking questions sometime around Year 130 YSL. The bottle arrived in Fluffington's quarters six hours later. He did not open it. He did not throw it out either. He set it on his desk next to the previous one hundred and ninety-six unopened bottles, which he kept [in a rack](ow://language/0bedcb3a-b972-4557-b4f8-5c701a5d04cb) he had commissioned for that purpose.

Narrative.name: Fluffington Demands Access
Narrative.description: Admiral Fluffington invokes a Treaty Council clause not cited in one hundred and ninety-seven years. The Keeper of Seals takes six days to find the key.
Narrative.story: The clause was Article 9, Section 4, Subsection B. It permitted the standing Admiral of the Puddle Navy to demand access to any Treaty Council-controlled facility on national-security grounds, subject to a unanimous Council vote within seventy-two hours, with the demand to be presented in person and in writing. Fluffington wrote it out by hand at oh-five-twelve on a Tuesday. He presented it at oh-eight-hundred. The Council was unanimous within forty minutes, which was the first unanimous Council vote in eighty-four years. The Keeper of Seals received the unanimous vote at oh-eight-forty-six. She began searching for the key at oh-eight-forty-seven. She did not find it. She kept searching. She did not eat that day. The next day she searched her own office twice. The day after that she went to her predecessor's old office, which had been vacant for thirty years. The day after that she went to her predecessor's predecessor's office, which had been vacant for eighty, and was used as a supply closet. The day after that she broke the lock on the supply closet drawer. The day after that she found the key wrapped in a piece of lavender silk-blend fabric with a triple-weave reinforcement. She unwrapped it and looked at the key for some time before she carried it out of the closet.

Narrative.name: Fluffington Receives
Narrative.description: Squeaky brings the three-word transmission to the Admiral's bridge station. The deep voice does not help.
Narrative.story: Squeaky read the transmission aloud at his normal volume, which was the volume of someone announcing a structural failure to a deaf engineering crew. The bridge went quiet. Rudder did not turn from the helm. Doc Stitch, who happened to be on the bridge picking up a routine felt-tear report, sat down on the floor next to the helm console without seeming to decide to. Commander Vera went on standing at parade-rest with her hands at her sides, which was what Commander Vera always did when she did not know what was about to happen and wanted to look like she did. Admiral Fluffington took the transmission slate, read it, set it down, and read it again. The second reading took longer. The bridge crew watched the Medal of Damp Valor on his uniform reflect the overhead light as his chest moved. Eventually he said: acknowledge receipt. Then he said: do not respond. Then he stood there for some time.

Narrative.name: Fluffington Stops Wearing The Medal
Narrative.description: Doc Stitch finds the Medal of Damp Valor in the recycler. He does not return it.
Narrative.story: Doc Stitch worked the night shift on the USS Fuzzball's medical bay. He performed felt repairs on three crew members between twenty-two-hundred and oh-four-hundred and at oh-four-twelve he went to the recycler to dispose of a damaged felt patch. The recycler chute had a small object resting on the diverter plate that had not yet been ground down. Doc Stitch reached in. He pulled out the Medal of Damp Valor. He looked at it. He looked at it for a longer time than he had spent looking at any object on the ship that was not a patient. He did not put it back in the recycler. He did not return it to the Admiral. He took it to his quarters and placed it in a drawer that already contained two other objects: a pressed flower from the Naval Academy garden, which had been pressed in Year 156 YSL, and a letter he had never sent to his brother, who had been killed at Damp Ridge. He closed the drawer. He went back to medical.

Narrative.name: Fluffington Visits Drizzle
Narrative.description: First time at The Soggy Sock since The Incident. He sits at the corner booth. He does not say what he came to say.
Narrative.story: Admiral Fluffington entered The Soggy Sock at twenty-one-fourteen wearing civilian felt and no rank insignia. He sat at Snoot's corner booth, which Snoot was not occupying that night, again, because Snoot had been at the Treaty Council most evenings. Drizzle brought a felted-rye to the booth without being asked. The glass was full. It was not watered. Drizzle had not watered an Admiral's drink in two hundred and three years. Fluffington took the glass. He drank it in three swallows. He set the glass down. He said: my father is dead. Drizzle said: I know. Fluffington said: I do not know what to do. Drizzle said: you do not have to know yet. Fluffington sat in the booth for forty-six minutes. Drizzle brought him a second drink. This one was watered. Fluffington did not notice or did not say. He left at twenty-two-oh-five. Drizzle did not refuse his payment. She did not accept it either. She put the credits in the jar marked tips, which was the jar marked tips because she did not have a jar marked truce.

Narrative.name: Joint Expedition Departs
Narrative.description: The USS Fuzzball and the Stale Vengeance leave Feltropolis docked alongside each other for the first time in moppet history. Crew transfers happen. Sergeant Flop and Nibbles end up on the same ship.
Narrative.story: The two ships left dock at oh-six-hundred on Year 203 YSL day three hundred and one, with cookie material and felt-laminate hulls less than four meters apart. The crew transfers had been negotiated over six weeks by Captain Snoot acting as nominal liaison, with Madame Threadbare handling the actual list-making. Sixteen Cookie Pirates boarded the USS Fuzzball. Sixteen Puddle Navy crew boarded the Stale Vengeance. Sergeant Flop, Marine Commander, was on the transfer list for the Vengeance, against his stated preference, by direct order from Fluffington. Nibbles, Quartermaster, was on the transfer list for the Fuzzball, at his own request, which the Crumbler had granted without comment. Flop and Nibbles passed each other on the docking bridge. Neither acknowledged the other. They had never met. They would, by the end of the voyage, have met thirty-four times and shared a wafer-ledger entry.

Narrative.name: Madame Threadbare Adjusts Her Inventory
Narrative.description: The fabric sample shipments to The Claw stop. The fabric sample shipments to Captain Snoot double. Nobody asks why; Madame Threadbare runs The Thread Market and inventory adjustments are her authority.
Narrative.story: The samples were lavender silk-blend with a triple-weave reinforcement, which The Claw had been receiving every eleven days since Year 154. The first missed shipment was on Year 203 YSL, day forty-two. The second missed shipment was day fifty-three. By the third missed shipment The Claw had logged it as a supply chain disruption and assigned three junior agents to investigate the Moisture Merchants Guild for interference, which was incorrect. The shipments to Captain Snoot, which had previously been one envelope per month containing a piece of fabric small enough to chew, became two envelopes per month containing pieces of fabric large enough to wrap a small object. The fabric was lavender silk-blend with a triple-weave reinforcement. Snoot did not eat them.
