Narrative.name: Old Biscuit Translates
Narrative.description: The Crumbler's oldest crewmate sits with the fragment for nine hours. He emerges saying: they remember being us.
Narrative.story: Old Biscuit was given the fragment in Pip's workbench room at zero-nine-hundred. He sat with it on his lap, in a chair that was not designed for sitting that long, for nine hours and seventeen minutes. He did not eat. He did not drink. He did not speak. Pip, who was present for the first hour as an observer, left at ten-hundred to perform routine duties and returned at eighteen-hundred to find Old Biscuit unchanged in position. At eighteen-seventeen Old Biscuit set the fragment down on the workbench. He stood up slowly, because nine hours in a non-designed chair had effects on felt circulation. He turned to Pip. He said: they remember being us. He sat back down. He did not say anything else for the rest of the day. The next day he asked Pip what cardamom smelled like. Pip did not know. Old Biscuit said: I think I do.

Narrative.name: Pip Drinks First
Narrative.description: The youngest moppet present takes the first absorption, by tradition. Pip drinks from a Bakerfolk source. Nothing visible happens.
Narrative.story: The tradition of the youngest moppet absorbing first had been written down in Year 12 YSL and had been honored at every source-opening since. There had been four prior source-openings, all on Puddleton or in immediate orbit. The fifth was inside The Rolling Pin. The youngest moppet present was Lieutenant Pip, age thirty-one, who had been the youngest on the bridge of the USS Fuzzball for nine years and would remain so for another three. She removed her absorption-suit faceplate. She placed her cheek against the receptacle, which was the standard absorption posture. She absorbed for the standard six seconds. The receptacle dispensed liquid. The liquid was clear. It absorbed into Pip's felt at the standard rate. Her felt did not change color. Her googly eyes did not still. The flavor receptors on her cheek registered cinnamon, butter, and a third taste that did not have a registered name in the moppet flavor catalog. She stepped back. She said: it is water. Then she said: also it is not. Doc Stitch, present at her insistence, ran every standard panel. Every standard panel returned within nominal parameters. Pip drank twice more. The second absorption was also water. The third absorption was also water. The third absorption also caused her, for the first time in her recorded life, to laugh, which she did not explain and which she did not do again that day.

Narrative.name: Pip's Acceleration Theory
Narrative.description: Pip revises her failure estimate. The number is worse than the previous number, which was already bad.
Narrative.story: Pip had estimated, based on her original five-year dataset, that the Eternal Drip would fail completely in approximately six hundred years. The revised estimate, after adding the post-fragment data and the fluctuation pattern from The Drippers' records, was between ten and thirty years. The new estimate was on a piece of recycled felt-paper, fourteen by twenty centimeters, drawn in three pencils because she had broken two more during the revision. She presented it to Admiral Fluffington at oh-eight-thirty. Fluffington looked at the new graph for ninety seconds, which was the same amount of time he had looked at the previous one. He asked one question: is this the worst case. Pip said: no. Fluffington said: thank you, Lieutenant. The ready room door closed behind her. It stayed closed for one hundred and twenty minutes. When it opened, Fluffington came out and walked directly to the bridge and ordered a fleet-wide signal that read: prepare expedition manifest. Captain Snoot consulting.

Narrative.name: Pip Tells Fluffington
Narrative.description: Pip stands in the Admiral's ready room with a notebook and a graph. She does not say the words civilization-ending. She says the words point three percent.
Narrative.story: Pip's graph was on a piece of recycled felt-paper, fourteen by twenty centimeters, drawn in two pencils because her primary pencil had broken on day fifty-one of the project and the replacement pencil drew slightly thicker lines, which Pip had compensated for by re-drawing the entire Year 198 to Year 201 segment, which had taken her three nights. The graph showed a slope. The slope was small. Fluffington looked at the slope for ninety seconds. He asked one question: is it accelerating. Pip said: I am collecting more data. Fluffington said: thank you, Lieutenant. The ready room door closed behind her and stayed closed for forty minutes.

Narrative.name: Professor Fuzz Looks Up From His Files
Narrative.description: Professor Fuzz finishes the Moistened Valley casualty discrepancy paper. He notices, for the first time in forty years, that someone has been following him.
Narrative.story: Professor Fuzz finished the paper at fourteen-twenty-seven on a Tuesday. He stood up from his desk, which he did not often do during a research day, and walked to the archive coffee machine, which had been broken since Year 191 YSL and which he kept walking to anyway out of habit. He poured himself a cup of nothing. He drank the cup of nothing. He returned to his desk. On the way back he passed the same brown-felted moppet he had been passing for forty years in the archive corridor and registered, for the first time, that this moppet had also been passing him every working day for those forty years and was not an archive staff member. Professor Fuzz did not change his expression. He sat down at his desk. He filed the paper in the wrong drawer on purpose. He went home through a route he had not used since graduate school. The brown-felted moppet did not follow him. The Claw, however, did, through three other moppets stationed along the new route, none of whom Professor Fuzz noticed, because he had never been trained to look for surveillance and was only running on the half-remembered instinct of a student who had once stolen a library card.

Narrative.name: Puddle Futures Collapse
Narrative.description: Three of the fourteen licensed Moisture Merchants Guild stations open the morning below contract pressure. The Felt Exchange suspends Puddle Futures trading for nine hours, the first suspension in eighty years.
Narrative.story: Station Seven opened at zero-seven-hundred with a pressure reading of nine point four out of ten contracted bars. Station Eleven opened at zero-seven-oh-three with nine point one. Station Twelve, which was the largest of the fourteen and which served the Naval Academy as well as the residential blocks on Level 4, opened at zero-seven-oh-five with eight point seven, which was the lowest opening reading in eighty years and below the regulatory threshold that should have triggered an automatic Guild audit, which it did not, because the regulatory threshold had been quietly lowered in Year 197 YSL by the Guild itself during a budget reallocation that nobody had read carefully. The Felt Exchange opened at zero-eight-hundred and closed at zero-eight-oh-three. The chair of the Exchange, who had been chair for thirty-one years and who had never closed the Exchange before, sat at her desk for the duration of the closure and did not eat lunch. Nibbles, watching from the Stale Vengeance's intercept array three days out from the Crumblefield buffer line, noted the closure in his wafer-ledger at the precise moment it occurred. He had been expecting it for six months.

Narrative.name: Snoot Brings The Evidence
Narrative.description: The hidden proof Captain Snoot has carried since Year 120 YSL arrives at the Council chamber, wrapped in fabric. Felt witnesses fabric.
Narrative.story: Snoot had carried the evidence in eleven different containers over eighty years. The current container was a felt-cured satchel with a false bottom that he had commissioned in Year 178 YSL from a craftsman who had then immediately died, which Snoot had not arranged but had not regretted. Inside the false bottom were three documents and a single recording crystal. The documents were the Year 0 YSL operations log of the second engagement, the casualty manifest signed by Stuffington, and a personal letter from Splashworth to his sister, dated three days before his death, which contained a sentence that no other surviving document contained. The crystal was the bridge audio from Splashworth's death. Snoot had listened to it once. He had not listened to it since. He wrapped the documents and crystal in a piece of lavender silk-blend with a triple-weave reinforcement, which he had received that morning. He carried the package to the Council chamber. He set it on the table. He sat down. He waited. The Council unwrapped the package. The Keeper of Seals, who had not let go of the key since finding it, recognized the fabric on sight. She did not say anything. She made a note in her own private ledger, which nobody else had ever read.

Narrative.name: Snoot's Counter-History
Narrative.story: Not a book. Not a document. A collection of things Captain Snoot carries: a fragment of evidence hidden somewhere on his person or behind a loose panel in The Soggy Sock, conversations with Drizzle that she will neither confirm nor deny, navigational logs from Year 118-120 that show the USS Splashworth's actual course during the final engagement, and a growing certainty that the Moistened Valley Massacre was ordered from above and buried by treaty. Snoot does not tell this story in sequence. He tells it in pieces, to people he half-trusts, in bars, after drinks that Drizzle waters down because she needs him functional. Madame Threadbare has heard more of it than anyone and sells fragments to both sides -- she considers this a public service, like a library that charges admission. Professor Fuzz has independently reconstructed about 40% of it from archival gaps and does not know the other 60% is drinking three levels below his apartment. If you laid Snoot's pieces next to Fuzz's gaps, the picture would be complete. They have never been in the same room. Madame Threadbare has considered introducing them. She has not yet decided what that introduction is worth.
Narrative.consequences: The most dangerous collection of facts in moppet civilization, held together by alcohol and stubbornness. If Snoot and Fuzz ever actually compared notes, the Treaty Council would face its first existential crisis in two centuries. The Claw knows this. They watch Snoot. They watch Fuzz. They have not yet realized that Madame Threadbare is the bridge, or that she charges by the thread. The counter-history has no title, no conservator, no institutional backing. It lives in one faded blue moppet who left the Navy rather than keep the secret, and in the silence of a gray bartender who saw what he describes and pours drinks to forget what she remembers.

Narrative.name: Stuffington Speaks
Narrative.description: The Locked Room opens. Admiral Stuffington has not spoken since Year 5 YSL. He says six words. Then nothing else.
Narrative.story: The Locked Room was smaller than anyone had remembered. The door was fifteen centimeters thick and made of felt-laminate over a steel core. The hinges had been oiled twice in two hundred years, by a maintenance subroutine that had been programmed into the station before anyone alive could remember the programmer. When the Keeper of Seals turned the key, the hinges did not creak. The room inside was lit by a single overhead lamp that had been left on since Year 0 YSL and that had cost the Treaty Council, by current accounting, three point seven million credits in electricity over the intervening period. Admiral Stuffington was sitting at a small desk. He had a chair. He had a bed. He had a sink. The Treaty Council had provided one book, which had been the same book for two hundred years, and which Stuffington had not opened in fifty. He was small. His felt had gone dry, not gray, which was a kind of decoloration Doc Stitch would later describe as without precedent. His googly eyes were still. He looked at Fluffington. He did not look at Snoot. He did not look at the Keeper of Seals. He said: the bakers are not gone. He stopped. The Council and the Admiral and the Captain and the Keeper all waited. Stuffington did not say anything else, that day or any day after. He died seven months later in his sleep. The book on his desk, when finally opened, turned out to be a Year 0 YSL edition of the Cookie Pirate Code, which he had not been authorized to possess and which the Treaty Council quietly removed from the inventory log.

Narrative.name: The Ballad of Splashworth
Narrative.story: The public legend of Admiral Splashworth, Hero of the Founding. Exists in at least six versions: a shanty sung in Navy mess halls that rhymes valor with sailor and gets worse from there; a children's felt-puppet show performed annually at the Academy in which tiny Splashworth defeats a cookie ten times his size; a bronze plaque beneath the Drip Plaza statue; a chapter in the Naval History of Moppetopia authored by the Treaty Council Historical Committee; a drinking song popular at The Soggy Sock that Drizzle refuses to serve during; and a commemorative absorption ceremony in which young cadets dip their left hand in water blessed at the Eternal Drip. None of these six versions agree on how Splashworth actually died. The shanty says he fell fighting. The puppet show says he sacrificed himself to save the Drip. The plaque says he gave his life for the future of all moppets. The drinking song, which is the oldest version, has a verse about the eye that saw too much that nobody can explain and everyone assumes is about a telescope. The ceremony involves closing your left eye. Nobody remembers why.
Narrative.consequences: Splashworth is the most recognized name in moppet history and the least understood person. His compass is on a flagship commanded by his murderer's grandson. His left googly eye is in that grandson's skull. His statue in Drip Plaza may be hollow -- there are rumors of something sealed inside during construction, but the statue was commissioned by the Treaty Council and questioning a public monument is considered poor form. He is beloved. He is also, in a sense that would horrify every moppet who sings about him, still trying to speak.

Narrative.name: The Crumbler at The Soft Spot
Narrative.description: Final pilgrimage before the crossing. The new pirates kneel in the residual warmth. Old Biscuit remembers a recipe his mother never wrote down.
Narrative.story: The Soft Spot was the only place in the Snack Nebula where the cookies had not gone stale. The pilgrims approached in pairs, by tradition, with their helmets off, by tradition, breathing the air that was warmer than it should have been and that smelled of butter and sugar and something else nobody had ever named. The new pirates, who were six in number this trip, knelt at the inner ring. They were each given a single uncrumbled biscuit from the ship's stores. They each ate it. Old Biscuit, who had been on every pilgrimage since Year 14 YSL, watched the new ones and remembered his mother, who had been a baker before the Treaty and who had taught him three recipes in the last week of her life, none of which she had written down. He had successfully reproduced two. The third he had been trying to reconstruct for one hundred and seventy years. He thought, kneeling at the inner ring with butter smell in his felt, that the third recipe involved cardamom. He had never thought this before. He filed it in the part of his head where he kept things that the Whispering had given him.

Narrative.name: The Drip Stops
Narrative.description: Year 203 was the year someone finally measured. Pip kept a notebook nobody read. Snoot brought back a fragment nobody asked for. The Crumbler sent a three-word message nobody knew how to answer. Then the percentages started moving faster.
Narrative.story: A six-chapter account of the Eternal Drip crisis, Year 203 to 210 YSL. Begins with the Soggy Sock Incident and ends with the first moppet to drink from a Bakerfolk source. Compiled from Puddle Navy logs, Cookie Pirate cookie-substrate inscriptions, Madame Threadbare's invoice book, and Pip's private notebook (released posthumously by her own request, though she is still alive at time of compilation, which is the kind of thing Pip thinks to specify in advance)..
Narrative.consequences: End of the two-hundred-year cover-up. Reopening of Bakerfolk contact. First inter-civilizational absorption protocol. Cookie Pirates lose their criminal designation by Year 215. Admiral Fluffington steps down by Year 219 and is not replaced; the Puddle Navy enters a long quiet period that the histories will eventually call the Second Long Peace, though nobody at the time calls it anything because nobody at the time believes it will last.

Compiled from Puddle Navy logs, Cookie Pirate cookie-substrate inscriptions, Madame Threadbare's invoice book, and Pip's private notebook (released posthumously by her own request, though she is still alive at time of compilation, which is the kind of thing Pip thinks to specify in advance)..

Narrative.name: The Drippers Confirm
Narrative.description: A small cabal of Felt Exchange traders, who have been watching the same fluctuations from the financial side, finally compares notes with Pip.
Narrative.story: The Drippers had four members. They met every fourteenth day in a back room of The Felt Exchange that was technically part of the absorption-station maintenance closet. They had been meeting for nine years. Three of the four had assumed for those nine years that the small price oscillations they were tracking were market noise. The fourth, whose name was Klepp and who had a daughter Pip's age, had not assumed this. When Pip's notebook excerpt reached him through Madame Threadbare's regular channels, he read it once and shut the office door. The other three Drippers arrived for the regular meeting eleven hours later and found Klepp had taken every chart off the wall and laid them on the floor in date order. They sat on the floor with him. They were on the floor when the morning bell rang.

Narrative.name: The Failing
Narrative.story: A spreadsheet. Technically. Pip started tracking the Eternal Drip's pressure readings five years ago because she was bored on night watch and the instrument panel had a decimal readout nobody else looked at. The first year showed 0.3% decline. She assumed measurement error. The second year showed 0.3% decline. She recalibrated the instruments. The third year showed 0.3% decline and she stopped sleeping well. By Year 431 she had mapped the decline curve, cross-referenced it with historical flow records she sweet-talked out of the Museum of Moistened History filing clerk -- the same filing system that loses Professor Fuzz's requests works fine for a nervous yellow moppet who brings baked goods -- and projected a failure date she has written on a scrap of felt she keeps folded in her left pocket. She has not told anyone on the USS Fuzzball. She has not told Admiral Fluffington. She mentioned it once to Nibbles during a supply exchange at the edge of the Crumblefields, and Nibbles -- who counts every crumb because the universe is only honest at the decimal level -- looked at the numbers and said 'Oh.' They sat in silence for four minutes. On a ship-to-ship channel between a Navy navigator and a Cookie Pirate quartermaster, four minutes of silence is either an act of war or an act of trust. It was trust. Somewhere in the Feltropolis commodity pits, Damp Margot and The Drippers are seeing the same curve from the financial side -- water futures ticking down, absorption ritual attendance steady, the gap between what the numbers say and what the culture believes growing wider by the quarter. They have never met Pip. The distance between these two datasets is the width of a civilization's remaining denial.
Narrative.consequences: The youngest crew member on the flagship and a fired accountant turned pirate quartermaster are the only two people who understand that moppet civilization has an expiration date. The Drippers are the only others who sense it, and they are using the knowledge to make money rather than sound alarms, because alerting the market would collapse their positions and nobody would believe them anyway. When these threads converge -- and they will, because numbers do not care about social strata -- the Eternal Drip stops being sacred and starts being a machine that someone needs to fix. The Bakerfolk built it. The Whispering might know how. But the people who hear the Whispering and the people who track the numbers have not yet found each other. Pip's scrap of felt and Damp Margot's ledger are two halves of the same alarm, folded in different pockets, in different parts of the station, waiting.

Narrative.name: The Failing Numbers
Narrative.description: Pip's notebook reaches the right hands. The Felt Exchange does math it has not had to do in eighty years and does not enjoy the result.
Narrative.story: There is a moment in any closed economy when the spreadsheet stops being a spreadsheet and becomes a confession. The Felt Exchange had been in that state for forty months by the time Pip's notebook arrived in the right office. The arrival did not cause the failure. It only made it visible.
Narrative.consequences: Puddle Futures suspend trading for the first time since the post-Treaty stabilization. The Drippers come out of cover. Professor Fuzz attracts more attention than he can detect.

Narrative.name: The First Drink From Cinnamon
Narrative.description: The expedition sails. Two civilizations meet for the second time, knowing the first time was a war. The youngest moppet drinks first, by tradition.
Narrative.story: Tradition required the youngest moppet present to take the first absorption from any new source. The tradition had been written into the absorption rituals in Year 12 YSL and had been honored at every source-opening since, of which there had been four, all of them on Puddleton or in Puddleton's immediate orbital range. The fifth source-opening was three weeks' sail past the Crumblefields, inside a humming ruin three kilometers long, beside a Bakerfolk receptacle that lit from within when the Rolling Pin Fragment was placed into it. The youngest moppet present was Pip. She drank.
Narrative.consequences: Pip's felt did not change color. Her googly eyes did not still. Nothing happened, which was the most unexpected thing that could have happened. The Bakerfolk source was, by every measurable test, water. It tasted of cinnamon. Both facts were recorded in the expedition log. Fluffington's revised fleet doctrine, transmitted on the return voyage, read: we sail where the puddles flowed. The past tense was deliberate.

Narrative.name: The Fragment Cools
Narrative.description: Pip's third night with the fragment from The Rolling Pin. She is alone in the workbench room on USS Fuzzball's engineering deck, watching the cinnamon smell fade and a temperature graph she has been drawing in pencil.
Narrative.story: The fragment lost warmth on schedule. Not the schedule of any cooling object Pip had ever measured, but the schedule of the Eternal Drip's pump cycle, which she had memorized at fourteen and not stopped tracking since. The fragment did not cool toward room temperature. It cooled in pulses. Eighteen minutes of decline, four seconds of holding, eighteen minutes of decline. The room temperature itself was sixteen point two degrees, which was the room temperature of every [Puddle Navy](ow://institution/73493c50-befe-40aa-8ff0-5db36abcbd7e) engineering deck for the past hundred and eighty years, because that was the temperature at which felt did not absorb extra moisture during routine wear. The fragment was at twenty-one point eight degrees and falling. Pip wrote down twenty-one point eight. She did not drink the tea she had made. She did not drink the second cup either. She made a third cup at oh-three-fourteen and at oh-three-thirty-two the fragment held at twenty point zero degrees and the smell of cinnamon, which had been faint for an hour, became briefly strong again, then went away. Pip wrote down: it is still doing something.

Narrative.name: The Fragment Hums
Narrative.description: The Rolling Pin Fragment, on Pip's workbench, begins emitting a tone below moppet hearing. Coravel schools outside Feltropolis turn and swim toward The Soft Spot.
Narrative.story: The fragment had been silent for one hundred and forty-three days. The hum, when it started, was at four hertz, which was below the auditory range of every moppet ever recorded. Pip detected it on a borrowed seismograph she had requisitioned from Geological Survey under a false name. The seismograph drew a clean sine wave. Pip recorded the start time: oh-three-fourteen on Year 203 YSL day two hundred and twelve. The hum continued. At oh-three-forty-six, the Feltropolis aquaculture monitor logged a sudden migratory pattern in the local Coravel schools, which had been stable for ninety years. The schools, which numbered approximately fourteen thousand individuals across six different feeding grounds, all turned within a four-minute window and began swimming on a heading of two-seventy-one point three degrees. This heading, when extended on a stellar chart, terminated at The Soft Spot. The aquaculture monitor flagged the event as anomalous. The flag was reviewed by a junior analyst who classified it as a seasonal pattern despite no precedent. The classification was filed at oh-four-twenty-two. The Coravel kept swimming.

Narrative.name: The Locked Room Opens
Narrative.description: Two hundred years of institutional cover-up cracks. Admiral Stuffington, who has not spoken since Year 5 YSL, speaks. He says six words, then stops.
Narrative.story: The Treaty Council had three keys to The Locked Room. Two of them had been lost. The third had been with the Keeper of Seals, an office that rotated every fifty years and had not been audited for key-possession since Year 87. It took the Keeper six days to find the key. She found it in a drawer in her predecessor's predecessor's office, which she did not have a key to and had to break the lock on, which was witnessed by Captain Snoot, who had been waiting on a hard bench outside the drawer-office for the entire six days because he had said he would and because there was no other place in Feltropolis where he would rather be sitting.
Narrative.consequences: Admiral Stuffington's six words: the bakers are not gone. The Treaty Council fractures along generational lines within seventy-two hours. Fluffington stops wearing the Medal of Damp Valor.

Narrative.name: The Moistened Valley Account
Narrative.story: The official history of the founding war, as preserved in Treaty Hall and taught at the Naval Academy. In this version: the Dry Ones attacked first. Admiral Stuffington led a heroic defense. Splashworth fell in the final battle, a martyr whose sacrifice turned the tide. The Treaty of Soft Landings was a generous peace extended by the victors to the vanquished. The Moistened Valley was where the decisive engagement occurred -- nothing more, nothing less, certainly not a massacre. Every year at the Year Zero Anniversary, the Treaty Council reads selections aloud in Drip Plaza while moppets absorb ceremonial moisture and feel proud. The Account has been revised fourteen times. Each revision removed something. Nobody has ever added anything back. The earliest version, handwritten on water-treated felt and stored in the Museum of Moistened History, is available for public viewing. It is displayed behind glass so thick that the actual text is unreadable. This is considered adequate preservation.
Narrative.consequences: Two hundred years of institutional stability built on a document that gets thinner every decade. Professor Fuzz has requested access to the original fourteen times. Each request was processed, filed, and lost by a filing system that works perfectly for everything else. Governor Dampworth once quoted from the Account at a Year Zero banquet and got two facts wrong. Nobody corrected him, partly out of politeness and partly because the correct facts had been removed in revision nine.

Narrative.name: The Rolling Pin Receives Them
Narrative.description: Three kilometers of humming ancient infrastructure. The fragment, returned, slides into a receptacle that was not visible until it was touched. The Rolling Pin lights up from inside.
Narrative.story: The Rolling Pin had been humming for two hundred years. The hum, on close approach, resolved into a chord. The chord had three notes. The notes did not correspond to any frequencies in the moppet auditory range or in any standard scale used by moppet musicians, which was a fact established by Communications Officer Squeaky during the approach using the Fuzzball's signal analyzer, which Squeaky had requested to operate in deep voice mode for personal reasons. The fragment was carried into the ruin by Pip, who had requested the duty. The receptacle was on the inner wall of what appeared to be an absorption chamber. It was not visible from any angle in the chamber. It became visible when Pip's gloved hand passed within four centimeters of the wall, at which point a circular indent appeared, the exact diameter of the fragment. Pip placed the fragment into the indent. The Rolling Pin lit from within. The light was not from any external source. The walls themselves began to emit, in a yellow-brown shade that smelled, through the suit recyclers, of cinnamon and butter. The chord did not change. The hum did not stop. A second sound joined it, lower, which Squeaky later identified as the absorption-cycle initial pressurization.

Narrative.name: The Whispering Answers
Narrative.description: The Soft Spot stops being silent. Pip's calculations get worse. Coravel schools change direction.
Narrative.story: The Whispering had been described, by the moppets who claimed to hear it, as a low continuous attention. Not a voice. The condition of being listened to. The Crumbler had heard it for sixty years. Old Biscuit had heard it for thirty. After the Rolling Pin Fragment was returned to its receptacle in Chapter Six, several other moppets began hearing it too, including Doc Stitch, who took early retirement, and Pip, who took notes.
Narrative.consequences: Old Biscuit's translation of the fragment's tone: they remember being us. Pip's revised failure estimate: ten to thirty years, possibly faster. Fluffington visits The Soggy Sock for the first time since The Incident.

Narrative.name: The Whispering Chronicle
Narrative.story: Nobody wrote this. Nobody tells it. It tells itself, from inside the cookie substrate of the Snack Nebula, in frequencies that feel like remembering something you never experienced. The Bakerfolk were here before moppets. They built the Eternal Drip, the Rolling Pin, the ovens that still hum at The Soft Spot. They are gone in every way that matters except that their minds persist in compressed cookie material -- dreaming in crumbs, lonely beyond what language can hold, and hungry to be remembered by anyone soft enough to hear them. The Crumbler hears them. Makes pilgrimages to The Soft Spot and sits for hours in the warm chewy anomaly, helmet off, macaron crust cooling. Comes back with information nobody asked for and nobody can verify. Pip heard them once, when she held the Fragment, and her googly eyes went completely still for ten seconds. Eyes do not do that. Old Biscuit claims the Whispering told him the recipe for immortality but he forgot it because he was also being told the recipe for a decent scone and got confused. He insists both were clearly labeled but the Whispering does not use labels. The Chronicle is not a story with a beginning and end. It is a continuous murmur of a dead civilization that built the infrastructure the living depend on and would very much like someone to notice.
Narrative.consequences: The deepest knowledge in moppet space is held by minds preserved in biscuit debris that nobody in power takes seriously. The Bakerfolk built the machine that keeps everyone alive. The machine is failing. The Whispering may contain the instructions for fixing it. The only people who can hear it are a pirate captain who wears a fused macaron helmet, a nervous navigator whose eyes should not have gone still, and an elderly quartermaster who got distracted by pastry recipes. The Treaty Council classifies The Soft Spot as contested territory of no strategic value, which is the single most incorrect assessment in the history of moppet intelligence.

Narrative.name: Three Words Are A Lot
Narrative.description: The Crumbler's message lands. Fluffington reads it twice. The Claw reads it forty-seven times and still does not know what to do with it.
Narrative.story: The transmission was three words long and arrived through the Cookie Pirates' regular trade-channel, which had been used in the past two hundred years to send approximately one transmission, by the same sender, and that one had been an inventory complaint about a missing crate of dried apricots. So when the second transmission came, the channel was technically still open from the first. The Claw spent six weeks running it through their cryptography stack. The message was already in plain Standard. It said: we're coming home. Nobody on Feltropolis felt qualified to receive this.
Narrative.consequences: The Claw begins panicked surveillance expansion. Madame Threadbare stops sending fabric samples to one of her clients. Drizzle pours the anniversary drink three months early.

Narrative.name: We Sail Where The Puddles Flowed
Narrative.description: Fluffington transmits a fleet-wide signal with one letter changed. The new doctrine is past tense.
Narrative.story: The signal went out at fourteen-hundred on the return voyage, on all fleet frequencies and on the unencrypted civilian band, which was unusual. The text read: we sail where the puddles flowed. The change from present tense to past tense was small. It was small in the way that, two hundred years prior, the change from surrendering to surrendered had been small. Captain Snoot, on the bridge of the Fuzzball as observer, watched Fluffington type the message himself. Fluffington did not show it to him first. Fluffington pressed transmit. The signal reached Feltropolis four hours later. Drizzle, at The Soggy Sock, heard it from the ambient station feed at the bar. She set down the glass she was polishing. She did not pick it up again that shift. Madame Threadbare, at The Thread Market, was in the middle of a transaction. She paused. She completed the transaction. She set her ledger down. She walked to the back of the shop and stayed there for some time. Professor Fuzz heard it through his office speaker, which he had forgotten to turn off after the morning announcements. He stopped writing. He read the line on his paper one more time. He filed the paper, this time in the correct drawer, under M for Moistened, where it had always belonged.

Object.name: Deep Drip
Object.description: The Moisture Merchants Guild's premium product line. Marketed as 'pure Eternal Drip source water, naturally filtered through ancient geological formations' with a label featuring a stylized water drop and the words 'From the Heart of the World.' It's regular station water run through an extra pipe that adds trace minerals for taste. Costs 12 felt-marks per absorption -- four times the price of standard salted puddle. The moppets who buy it insist they can taste the difference. They can't. The extra pipe doesn't even connect to the Eternal Drip. The Guild knows this. The label designer knows this. Governor Dampworth drinks it exclusively and has given the Guild a commendation for 'excellence in hydration.' It is, after the Treaty of Soft Landings itself, possibly the most successful lie in moppet civilization.
Object.aesthetics: Elegant glass vessels with gold-leaf labeling. The stylized water drop logo. Premium felt-wrapped dispensers on Level 2.
Object.utility: Overpriced water. Status symbol. Proof that marketing works on moppets too.
Object.origins: Created by the Moisture Merchants Guild approximately 50 years ago. Has survived three attempted fraud investigations, each of which concluded that 'premium hydration perception is subjective.'

Object.name: Drip Drop
Object.description: Courier ship known for fast delivery.

Object.name: Felt Cruiser
Object.description: Standard military vessel class used by the Puddle Navy.

Object.name: Googly Eye of Truth
Object.description: Ancient precursor artifact - a First Fuzzy One's preserved consciousness in googly eye form. Possibly hidden in The Locked Room on Feltropolis Level 7, OR possibly in Snoot's eyepatch socket (he found it in Snack Nebula crash, traded it to Cookie Pirates for safe passage, they gave it back because The Crumbler couldn't bear its visions). If Snoot has it, this is why he sees things and drinks. Precursor to modern Googly Eye Technology.
Object.utility: Unknown. Shows visions of truth. Possibly contains advanced consciousness or navigation capabilities.
Object.origins: Created by the ancient Bakerfolk/First Fuzzy Ones civilization. Contains preserved consciousness.

Object.name: Medal of Damp Valor
Object.description: Puddle Navy military decoration featuring a three-splash insignia. Worn by Admiral Fluffington.

Object.name: Rolling Pin Fragment
Object.description: Fragment retrieved by Captain Snoot from The Rolling Pin ruin. Warm to the touch and smells of cinnamon. When Navigator Pip held it, her googly eyes went completely still for ten seconds . No moppet’s eyes do that. Pip’s subsequent calculations suggest the fragment’s resonance matches the Eternal Drip’s pump cycle, implying a connection between The Rolling Pin and the ancient water infrastructure.
Object.aesthetics: Warm, cinnamon-scented fragment of ancient Bakerfolk construction material.
Object.utility: Unknown. Resonance matches the Eternal Drip's pump cycle, which could mean it's a key to understanding or repairing the failing water system. Or it could mean something worse.

Object.name: Splashworth's Compass
Object.description: Old compass that belonged to Admiral Splashworth. Now carried by Admiral Fluffington as a sentimental artifact. Uncertain if it has special properties - possibly broken, possibly points to something significant, possibly points to the truth itself.
Object.utility: Navigation device. Possibly symbolic or magical guidance.
Object.origins: Belonged to Admiral Splashworth during The Great Puddle War.

Object.name: Stale Vengeance
Object.description: The Cookie Pirates' ship. Made from compressed cookie material - somehow space-worthy. Feltropolis engineers can't figure out how it works. Possibly uses ancient Bakerfolk technology. Capable of executing The Stale Roll - a spinning ramming maneuver that exploits the inexplicable hardness of aged cookie hull material. Feltropolis naval analysts have written four papers on why the maneuver shouldn't work. The Cookie Pirates have not read any of them.
Object.aesthetics: Constructed from compressed cookies - brown, textured, stale.

Object.name: The Fragment
Object.description: A piece of The Rolling Pin retrieved by Captain Snoot during his latest unauthorized expedition past the Crumblefields. Approximately fist-sized, warm to the touch, smells distinctly of cinnamon. Composition unknown - not felt, not cookie, not any material Feltropolis engineers recognize. When Pip held the Fragment near her instruments, her googly eyes went completely still for ten seconds - an involuntary response that shouldn't be physically possible. Her subsequent calculations revealed the Fragment's resonance frequency matches the Eternal Drip's pump cycle exactly. This is either the most important archaeological discovery in moppet history or the thing that destroys moppet civilization. Possibly both. Currently hidden somewhere on the USS Fuzzball, known only to Snoot, Pip, and Drizzle.
Object.utility: Proof that Bakerfolk technology underlies moppet infrastructure. Also: makes Pip's eyes do something impossible.
Object.origins: Bakerfolk construction. Retrieved from The Rolling Pin, Year 203 YSL.

Object.name: The Squeezed Sponge
Object.description: Merchant vessel operating in moppet space.

Object.name: USS Fuzzball
Object.description: Flagship of the Puddle Navy commanded by Admiral Fluffington.

Object.name: USS Splashworth
Object.description: Puddle Navy ship named posthumously after Admiral Splashworth as an honor. Naval tradition appears to be NOT naming ships after living admirals.

Phenomenon.name: Googly Eye Consciousness
Phenomenon.description: Googly eyes are functional organs connected to moppet consciousness and soul. The liquid inside contains the floating pupil and is linked to the moppet's sense of self. Pupil movements are involuntary responses - eyes wobble when moppets lie. Googly Eye Technology amplifies what's naturally there. Removing an eye is not just physical damage but soul damage - removing part of consciousness itself. Transplanted eyes carry fragments of previous owner's consciousness (Fluffington has Splashworth's left eye and experiences his memories).
Phenomenon.expression: Googly eyes function as both sensory organs and the primary interface for moppet consciousness. Pupil movement reflects emotional and mental state: a still eye is always a bad sign.
Phenomenon.effects: Removing an eye takes something out of a moppet that doesn't grow back. Transplanted eyes sometimes carry fragments of the previous owner's consciousness, which is either a gift or a haunting depending on who they were. Eyes can be calibrated and amplified for use in technology. Ancient eyes appear to preserve consciousness across long spans of time, which raises questions nobody in the Navy wants raised.
Phenomenon.mythology: Moppet eyes are where the soul actually lives. Not a metaphor. The Bakerfolk seem to have known this. Whether they built the googly eye for that reason, or discovered it by accident, is not recorded.

Relation.name: Fluffington-Snoot Rivalry
Relation.description: Not a petty graduation incident rivalry. The rivalry stems from Snoot discovering evidence of the Moistened Valley Massacre and wanting to tell the truth, while Fluffington wants to protect the Puddle Navy's reputation (and his father's memory - he's in denial about Stuffington's war crime). Snoot left the navy with proof hidden somewhere. Fluffington either knows the truth or just found out. The rivalry is about secrets, institutional loyalty versus truth, and the weight of generational trauma. They were friends, maybe more than friends, at Naval Academy. The betrayal broke both of them.
Relation.background: Began at or after The Incident (Year 120 YSL) when Snoot found evidence of the war crime. Both graduated from Naval Academy together but their paths diverged over how to handle the truth. Used to be friends or lovers.

Species.name: Bakerfolk
Species.description: Ancient pre-moppet civilization. Built the Eternal Drip machine and created the Snack Nebula ovens. Vanished - possibly evolved into moppets, ascended, or went extinct. No living examples. Evidence includes ancient artifacts, the Googly Eye of Truth, and architectural ruins in deep Puddleton caves. Their minds may be preserved in cookie substrate in the Snack Nebula (The Whispering).

Species.name: Coravel
Species.description: Space fish. Swim through vacuum somehow. Found near Feltropolis in schools. Considered good luck by spacers.
Species.appearance: Fish-like creatures that exist in vacuum.

Species.name: Dust Moppet
Species.description: Also called The Dry Ones. Not evil, just different absorption needs - they were starving during the war. Mostly integrated into moppet society after The Great Puddle War, though some holdouts exist in the Snack Nebula as Cookie Pirates. Their knowledge of surviving without water was suppressed after the Treaty.
Species.appearance: Rougher felt texture like burlap. Browns, tans, grays (natural coloring, not trauma-induced).
Species.instincts: Absorb minerals, dust, and dry particulates instead of moisture.
Species.communication: Googly eye movements, similar to Puddle Moppets.

Species.name: Feral Moppet
Species.description: Live in wild areas between settlements. Lost their googly eyes somehow and navigate by touch. Felt is matted and dirty. Terrifying to civilized moppets. Used by Cookie Pirates as scouts because they feel vibrations in crumbs. Two populations: born-feral and became-feral (who remember civilization and are sadder).
Species.appearance: Matted, dirty felt. No googly eyes.
Species.instincts: Navigate by touch instead of sight. Feel vibrations in surrounding materials.
Species.sociality: Live in wild areas, away from civilization.

Species.name: Puddle Moppet
Species.description: The standard moppet subtype. Water-absorbing, traditional, mostly found in Puddleton.
Species.appearance: Vibrant felt colors (pink, blue, orange, green, purple). Standard googly eyes that are functional organs, not decorations.
Species.instincts: Absorb moisture through felt. Drawn to water sources.
Species.communication: Googly eye pupil movements convey meaning and emotion.

Species.name: Space Moppet
Species.description: Evolved or adapted over 200 years in Feltropolis orbital station. Cultural or biological distinction unclear.
Species.appearance: Thinner, more vacuum-resistant felt. Paler, pastel colors. Slightly larger googly eyes, possibly adapted to station lighting.
Species.instincts: Can survive brief vacuum exposure (10-15 minutes).

Species.name: The Whispering
Species.description: Ancient Bakerfolk minds preserved in cookie substrate in the deep Snack Nebula. Not evil, just lonely. Hungry to be remembered. The Crumbler hears them. Speaks without speaking - non-physical or incorporeal communication.
Species.appearance: Unknown. Non-physical presence in cookie debris.
Species.communication: Speaks without speaking. Preserved consciousness communicating across time.

Title.name: Admiral
Title.authority: Highest rank in the Puddle Navy. Commands flagship and fleet operations.

Title.name: Chief Engineer
Title.authority: Oversees engineering operations and maintenance on naval vessels.

Title.name: Marine Commander
Title.authority: Leads boarding parties and shipboard security forces.

Title.name: Medical Officer
Title.authority: Provides medical care and felt repair to crew.

Title.name: Navigator
Title.authority: Responsible for ship navigation and course plotting.

Title.name: The Keeper of Seals
Title.authority: Unknown. Title exists in Puddle Navy hierarchy but function and current holder are undocumented.
Title.history: Mentioned in naval records but details lost or suppressed.

Title.name: Weapons Officer
Title.authority: Commands ship weapons systems and combat operations.

Trait.name: Resolute Dampness
Trait.description: Maintains optimal felt moisture under pressure. While other moppets wilt or dry out in crisis situations, Fluffington's felt stays immaculately hydrated: a      physical manifestation of his refusal to show weakness. Some interpret this as natural composure. Drizzle recognizes it as something else entirely: the body performing calm while the mind won't look at what's underneath.

Map.name: Crumblefields Survey Chart
Map.description: Cookie Pirate survey of the Crumblefield region, compiled by Nibbles' department over forty years. Includes crumb-density gradient overlays, buffer line, the Stale Vengeance's standard patrol routes, and approximate Crumb-Eel territories. The Puddle Navy does not have an equivalent chart and has not requested a copy.

Map.name: Feltropolis Station Schematic
Map.description: Multi-level schematic of Feltropolis orbital station. Seven levels: Docks (1), Commerce (2), The Squeeze (3), Residential (4), Administration (5), The Works (6), The Spire (7). Compiled from station engineering archives.

Map.name: MoppetopiaMap
Map.description: Overworld chart of the moppet civilization region: Puddleton homeworld, Feltropolis orbital station, the Snack Nebula and its Crumblefield approach, and the line where Naval patrols stop.

Marker.name: Pip's Workbench
Marker.description: Engineering deck workbench, USS Fuzzball. Where the Rolling Pin Fragment cooled in eighteen-minute pulses on three successive nights in Year 203 YSL. The seismograph that detected the four-hertz hum still sits at the north corner of this bench, returned by Geological Survey after they discovered the false-name requisition and decided not to pursue it.

Marker.name: Soggy Sock Booth
Marker.description: Captain Snoot's corner booth at The Soggy Sock tavern, Feltropolis Level 3. Snoot has occupied this booth between Year 121 YSL and present, with the exception of approximately forty-seven nights when he has been off-station. Drizzle does not seat other patrons here even when he is absent for months at a time.

Marker.name: Splashworth's Last Stand
Marker.description: Coordinates of Admiral Splashworth's death during the Moistened Valley Massacre. Killed by friendly fire on orders from Admiral Stuffington while attempting to halt the slaughter of surrendering Dust Ones forces. Officially commemorated as 'died in battle.' Unofficially marked on Cookie Pirate charts as 'the witness fell here.'

Marker.name: The Locked Door
Marker.description: Access point to The Locked Room, Feltropolis Level 7. Door is fifteen centimeters thick, felt-laminate over steel core. Opened only twice since Year 0 YSL: Year 5 (Stuffington's incarceration) and Year 203 (Stuffington's release). The overhead lamp inside has burned continuously between the two openings.

Marker.name: The Soft Spot Center
Marker.description: Inner ring of The Soft Spot, deep Snack Nebula. Sacred to the Cookie Pirates. Pilgrimage destination for new Pirates as initiation. Anomalous warmth has been measured at approximately two to four degrees above ambient and is consistent across the inner ring's diameter, which is approximately forty meters.

Zone.name: Crumblefields
Zone.description: Buffer region between Treaty space and the deep Snack Nebula. Compressed cookie material at variable density. De facto Cookie Pirate territory by mutual unspoken agreement since the Crumblefield Standoff.

Zone.name: Dry Ones Retreat Path
Zone.description: Route taken by surviving Dust Moppets from the Moistened Valley massacre site to the Snack Nebula in Year 0 to 4 YSL. Approximately three thousand individuals. The path is not maintained and is not marked on official maps; this rendering is reconstructed from Cookie Pirate accounts.

Zone.name: Eternal Drip Pipeline
Zone.description: Underground water conduit running from the Eternal Drip pumping station to the fourteen licensed Moisture Merchants Guild distribution points. Constructed by the First Fuzzy Ones at unknown date; uncovered and surveyed by moppets in Year 5 YSL.

Zone.name: Naval Patrol Border
Zone.description: Outer limit of standard Puddle Navy patrol coverage. Marks the boundary beyond which the Treaty does not require Naval response to civilian distress signals. The Cookie Pirates have informally extended their own patrols beyond this line since Year 203 YSL.

Zone.name: Puddleton Territory
Zone.description: Historic territory of the Puddle Moppets. Surface settlements, primary water reserves, and the original Naval Academy. Largely depopulated since the Felt Technology Revolution moved manufacturing to Feltropolis, though Puddleton remains the political capital and home of the Treaty Council.

Zone.name: Snack Nebula
Zone.description: Dangerous asteroid field of stale cookies. Refuge of the Cookie Pirates since Year 4 YSL. Contains The Soft Spot at its inner ring and The Rolling Pin three weeks' sail past the Crumblefield boundary.

Zone.name: Treaty Neutral Zone
Zone.description: Demilitarized region surrounding Feltropolis Station, established by Article 3 of the Treaty of Soft Landings. No military vessels permitted within radius. Enforced by Treaty Council inspection patrols, which have not encountered a violation in one hundred and ninety-seven years.
